- Melee combat: hold left click on a creature to strike. Damage depends on what you hold, with new wooden, stone, and iron swords hitting hardest. Hits knock creatures back, flash them red, and pop up damage numbers.
- Torches (stick + coal or cinder) and lanterns (iron ingot + torch at a workbench): walk-through light blocks with glowing flames and flickering light. No Ashen spawn within their reach.
- Deer and boar roam meadows and pine hollows by day. Deer bolt when you come close; boar charge back when hurt. Both give raw meat to cook in the furnace.
- Slain Ashen drop cinders: fuel for furnaces and torches.

**Limitations:** Creatures and world edits, torches included, last only for the session. Ashen pathing is greedy, so mazes and long walls can stall them. No sounds yet.

versions.title: Hunger under the ash
versions.notes:
- Health, hunger, stamina, and breath bars. Sprinting and jumping cost stamina, falls past three and a half blocks hurt, and you drown after ten seconds underwater. Starving hurts; staying fed heals.
- Death screen and respawning at your bed (right-click one to claim it) or the world spawn. You keep your pack.
- New items that aren't blocks: sticks, coal, iron ingots, plant fiber, bandages, berries, wild tubers, and raw and cooked meat. Right-click food to eat and bandages to heal.
- Inventory screen (E or Tab): 9 hotbar slots plus a 27-slot pack, with click, drag, half-split, place-one, and shift-click moves, and a recipe list for crafting.
- Wooden, stone, and iron pickaxes, axes, and shovels with mining-speed tiers and durability. Stone needs a pickaxe and iron ore a stone one, or nothing drops.
- Workbench for tools, furnaces, and beds. The furnace smelts iron ore, meat, tubers, cobblestone, and gravel, burning coal, wood, and sticks over time, even while you're away.
- Berry bushes in meadows and pine hollows. Leaves drop sticks and fiber, and grass sometimes turns up a wild tuber.
- Version Log screen in the pause menu.

**Limitations:** No animals yet, so raw meat can't be found until v0.1.2. Furnace contents and beds last only for the session.

versions.title: First light over the ash
versions.notes:
- Endless, seeded voxel world streamed in 16×64×16 chunks on worker threads, with meadows, pine hollows, ashlands, dunes, snowy peaks, shorelines, caves, ores, and three tree types.
- Face-culled meshing with baked ambient occlusion, per-voxel color variation, and translucent sea water.
- First-person walking, sprinting, jumping, swimming, and a debug fly mode.
- Hold-to-mine with per-block hardness, block drops, a 9-slot stacking hotbar, and block placement.
- Ten-minute day/night cycle with dusk-tinted sky, moonlight, matched depth fog, and drifting ash.

**Limitations:** No survival stats, crafting, enemies, or saving yet. Edits persist only while the session runs.

versions.title: Real squishing & order cards
versions.notes:
- The mortar has physics: ingredients tumble into the bowl and roll around. Grab the pestle by its handle and bring it down hard: three good smashes squish an ingredient flat. Sideways pushes just shove things along.
- Order cards: each waiting customer's order hangs on a rail on the wall. Tap one to make it the current order.
- Which Ingredients? spell (3 feathers): jars the current order needs glow.
- Best Ingredients spell (4 feathers): the jar tray lights up the ones that suit the current order.

**Limitations:** Ingredient spells need a current order picked on the rail.

versions.title: Stems & hats
versions.notes:
- Blue roots have a stem at one end: cut it off first (at mark 1), then cut the rest to size. A piece with the stem still on doesn't belong in the brew.
- The ruler now goes to 10.
- Hats: pick the wizard hat or the silly pinwheel hat (it spins) on the title screen.

**Limitations:** Only the blue root has a stem so far.

versions.title: Clock ticks & hardcore heat
versions.notes:
- Cooking time is now in clock ticks: the bigger wall clock has numbers 1–12, the hand moves one number per tick, and the face pulses at each one. The Stomach Ache Potion needs 2 ticks of heat.
- Heat counts by the level the thermometer has reached (4.9 is still 4), and time spent below a recipe's heat doesn't count.
- Hardcore mode (title screen): no thermometers, only flame color.
- Thermometer spell (3 feathers): brings the thermometers back for the day.
- Sweet Spot spell (5 feathers): thermometers mark the heat each brew needs.
- Casting a day-long spell that's already working doesn't use feathers.
- The clock moved next to the cauldrons so the jar tray can't cover it.

**Limitations:** The Blue Potion now cooks for 2 ticks (30 s) instead of 20 s.

versions.title: Feather spells
versions.notes:
- Tap the duck to open the feather mat. Tap spots to lay feathers down; when they make a spell's symbol, it's cast.
- Mistake Sight (3 feathers): notes say what went wrong with a brew. Without it, a mistake only turns the brew murky. On by default while debugging.
- Which Potion? (4 feathers): customers describing a problem narrow it down to two potions.
- The duck has 12 feathers a day; its tail thins as you spend them, and they grow back the next day.

**Limitations:** Losing feathers is only cosmetic for now.

versions.title: Choosing & cutting
versions.notes:
- Each jar holds a mix of its ingredient in different colors, spot counts, and sizes. Tap a jar to tip it out on a tray and pick the right ones.
- Cutting board with a ruler: drop a root on it and tap the ruler to cut at that mark. Bigger roots are longer.
- Recipes can name the color, spots, size, or piece length they need; the Stomach Ache Potion takes any ashberries.
- Mistakes say exactly what was off, like the wrong color or a piece of the wrong length.
- The flask rack moved onto the shelf to make room for the cutting board.

**Limitations:** The Blue and Green potions are still placeholders.

versions.title: What ails you
versions.notes:
- About half of customers describe their problem instead of naming a potion, so you work out which one helps.
- Each recipe page now says what the potion is for.
- The wrong potion for a described problem gets "That won't help with my problem."

**Limitations:** The Blue and Green potions still use placeholder ailments.

versions.title: Juggling & days
versions.notes:
- Two cauldrons, each with its own fire, bellows, and thermometer.
- Up to three customers wait at the window at once. Each slowly loses patience (watch their faces) and leaves if it runs out.
- Handing a real potion to the wrong customer: they say what they wanted instead, and it's thrown out.
- Days: the wall clock runs a 3-minute shift and the sign flips to Closed at the end. You can still serve whoever's waiting; once they're gone, the day ends.
- End-of-day summary: customers served, potions thrown out, and customers who left. Then on to the next day.
- Placeholder Blue Potion (heat between 3 and 6, 2–5 stirs) and Green Potion (very hot, 4+ stirs), with Blue Root and Green Leaf.
- The recipe book now sits on the shelf.

**Limitations:** Days don't carry anything over yet.

versions.title: The stomach ache potion
versions.notes:
- Customers come to the serving window and ask for a potion by name, one at a time.
- Recipe book on the counter: tap it to read how each potion is made.
- Stomach Ache Potion: squish 3 ashberries, put them in the cauldron, keep it at 5/12 heat or more for 30 seconds, stir at least 3 times, and pour it into a flask.
- Ingredient shelf, mortar and pestle (tap the pestle to pound), and a rack of empty flasks.
- Cauldron: pump the bellows to heat it, and it cools slowly. Flame color and the thermometer show the heat. Drag in circles to stir; each stir is counted and the swirl shows your speed. Tap the handle to tip it out.
- Mistakes show right away: the brew turns murky and a note says what went wrong.
- Drop a flask on the customer to hand it over. A wrong one is thrown out and they keep waiting. The bin takes anything.

**Limitations:** One cauldron and one customer at a time; no timers or days yet.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- Title screen with Open the shop and Version Log.
- Shop scene: the duck alchemist in a wizard hat behind the counter, an ingredient shelf, and a cauldron, all smooth 2D placeholders.
- All on-screen text comes from data/text.csv, tagged as AI- or Josh-written. Press F2 to mark AI text with [AI]; tools/audit_text.gd lists it.
- All art loads through data/art.csv. Set a row's path to a file to replace its placeholder.
- Mouse and touch both work. 1280×720 layout that stretches to fit the window.
- Web export to Exports/Potion Maker/v0.1.0.

**Limitations:** No customers or brewing yet; those start in v0.1.1.

versions.title: Camera fix
versions.notes:
**Camera fix (P2, reported by Josh from the web build).**

- **Bug:** randomly, the view flickered and the camera snapped to a different direction while playing the web build. Josh's guess was right: it's the pointer lock. On web, when pointer lock engages or re-engages (initial click, closing a menu, the browser recentering the cursor, focus changes), the browser fires a mouse-motion event whose delta is the recenter jump — potentially hundreds of pixels — and `player.gd` applied `event.relative` to the camera unfiltered.
- **Fix (in `player.gd`):** a pointer-lock spike guard for mouse look — (1) the first motion event after every transition into captured mode is dropped; (2) motion is ignored for 150 ms after capture or window-focus return; (3) any single event with a jump over 400 px on either axis is discarded as an artifact; (4) each event's look step is clamped to 150 px, so genuine fast flicks still register but can never teleport the view. No engine or export changes; the single-threaded preset is unchanged.
- Version bumped to 0.1.3 everywhere (VERSION, GameState.VERSION, HUD corner, in-game changelog); Web export preset now points at `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival/v0.1.3/`.

versions.title: Bugfix + save-slots update
versions.notes:
**Bugfix + save-slots update**, scoped from Josh's first playtest of the web build (2026-10-07 evening):

- **P0 — Ambient drone removed.** v0.1.1's synthesized ambient loop (a constant 55/110/165 Hz tone on the Music bus) is gone — there is no background tone at all now. All short SFX stay. The Music bus and slider remain in Settings, relabelled "reserved for future music".
- **P1 — Restart after death fixed.** The death restart polled `Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_R)` every frame and re-fired `reload_current_scene()` until the scene swapped, on top of a partial hand-reset of GameState. Now: a dedicated `restart` action with a just-pressed edge trigger, a `_restarting` guard, one deferred reload, and a new `GameState.reset_run()` that resets all run state (day 1, 08:00, kills/recruited/trees/crafted = 0). The death panel also has a visible **Restart (R)** button. `player.take_damage` no longer touches the pause flag — the HUD owns pausing.
- **P1 — Menu is Tab or Esc; C is crafting only.** New `menu` action on Tab + Escape; the old Tab crafting binding is deleted. Tab is handled in the HUD's `_input` (before GUI focus navigation, marked handled) because in a browser Esc exits pointer lock — Tab is the reliable menu key on web. Tab does not steal focus while typing a save name.
- **P1 — Melee rebalance (both directions).** Player reach: Fists 2.0→2.8, Bat 2.4→3.2, Spear 3.2→4.0, and zombie hits are measured to the zombie's surface (centre distance − 0.5) instead of its centre. Zombie attack range 1.6→1.25, attack cooldowns 0.9/1.0→1.2 s, and zombies now stop advancing 1.3 from their target instead of shoving into it. Net effect: every melee weapon can hit a zombie from outside its attack range.
- **P1 — Real pause in menus.** Any open panel (pause menu, crafting, help, settings, save, load, console, version log, death) now pauses the whole SceneTree — the world, zombies, survivors, and clock all freeze. The HUD layer runs with `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` so menus stay interactive; saving/loading from a panel closes panels and unpauses first, then runs deferred, so the game resumes into the loaded state.
- **P1 — Named save slots.** The single `user://savegame.json` slot is replaced by named files in `user://saves/<name>.json` (same payload plus a `slot_name` field). Names are sanitised (letters/digits/space/`_`/`-`, max 24 chars, empty rejected with a toast). Pause menu → Save Game (name field + click an existing name to overwrite) and Load Game (every slot listed with its Day and time, Load + Delete per slot). **v0.1.1's single save is not carried over.**
- **P2 — Quicksave slot.** F5 quicksaves and F9 quickloads the slot named `quicksave`; it appears in the Load list like any other slot. (On web, F5 reloads the page — use the pause-menu panels there.)

versions.title: Pollution patch
versions.notes:
"Pollution" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md). This is the run's builder's-choice version, and the final version of the run (v0.1.3–v0.1.8).

- **The choice, and why:** the remaining TODO items were weighed as the run's last slot. Multilayer building (P2) and trains, pipes/fluids, and multi-tile buildings (P3) are all multi-version structural projects — starting one as a single final version would ship it half-proven. **Pollution (P3)** is the one remaining item that is self-contained in a single version, and it was picked because it deepens the system the run just built (v0.1.6 evolution) instead of adding a parallel one, reuses the v0.1.7 statistics surface, gives the factory a real long-term tradeoff (output vs. biter pressure), and is fully harness-testable.
- **Pollution (new GameState state, saved):** working machines emit pollution at per-second rates (`POLLUTION_RATES`: furnace 0.020, boiler 0.015, miner 0.010, assembler 0.008, lab 0.005), counted in `main.simulate`'s per-building loop whenever a machine's `is_working` is set. The current level decays by 0.2% of itself per second (`tick_pollution`), so a small base stays near zero while a large factory's cloud lingers. GameState tracks both the current level and the lifetime emitted total. This implements the TODO P3 wording "pollution that scales biter waves with factory output" through the evolution channel: `pollution_factor()` = 1 + min(level, 100)/50 multiplies the time-based evolution creep (×1 clean, ×2 at 50, ×3 at the cap), and evolution in turn scales biter toughness, wave size, and speed — factory output now literally angers the biters faster. Nest kills and science consumption add their own evolution on top, unchanged.
- **UI:** the HUD top bar shows "Pollution: N" next to Evolution, the v0.1.7 Statistics panel gains "Pollution (current)" and "Pollution emitted (all time)" lines from `stats_text()`, and the Help text documents the system.
- **Save format:** saves gain `pollution` and `pollution_emitted`. v0.1.0–v0.1.7 saves still load (clean sky, nothing emitted).
- **Harness note (two adaptations):** the v0.1.7 checks that asserted the literal version string "0.1.7" (const + HUD label) now assert the durable invariant — the HUD corner label shows whatever `GameState.VERSION` currently is — with the literal asserted per release by that release's own checks (v0.1.8 (a) asserts "0.1.8"). No behavioural checks changed.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **300/300 checks passed** (all 285 v0.1.7 checks plus 15 new: version literal, the pollution factor curve at 0/50/100/500 including the ×3 cap, absorption decay math and its zero floor, machine emission over 3 simulated seconds against the boiler/miner world, the statistics pollution lines, the ~×3 evolution creep at 100 pollution, the top-bar readout, pollution save/load restoration against in-between mutations, and legacy saves without pollution keys loading with a clean sky). versions.title: Statistics + autosave patch
versions.notes:
"Statistics + autosave" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Statistics (new GameState state, saved):** a `stats` record in `scripts/game_state.gd` tracks `items_produced` (a per-item dict; the total is derived from it, so the two can never disagree), `biters_killed`, `buildings_placed`, `buildings_deconstructed`, `nests_destroyed`, `shots_fired`, and `playtime_seconds` (accumulated in `main.simulate`). Production is counted at the point of production: miner output and hand mining in main, furnace smelts and assembler crafts in their machine ticks, and hand-craft completions inside `GameState.tick_crafting` itself so every driver of the queue counts them exactly once. Placement counting sits in `place_building` behind a `count_stat` flag that save-loading passes as false (restoring a world is not placing), and deconstruction counts only the refunding player paths (hold channel / demolish mode) — biter destruction passes `refund=false` and does not count. Kills are counted at the two kill sites (turret tick, engineer shot), shots at the two firing sites (a shot that finds no target or no ammo does not count). Nest destruction counts in `damage_nest`.
- **Statistics panel:** the pause menu gains a **Statistics** button opening a scrollable panel rendered from `GameState.stats_text()` — headline counters, then the per-item production breakdown (most-produced first, name breaks ties, so the order is deterministic). The Help text documents it.

The autosave timer advances only while no modal is open, so a due autosave is **deferred** to the next quiet moment — it never fires under a menu and is never dropped. Restarting a world resets the timer.
- **Settings:** `user://settings.cfg` gains a `game` section holding `autosave_enabled` (default on), persisted by the same settings holder that keeps the audio keys (`scripts/sfx_player.gd`); loaded at startup, saved on change from the pause menu's **Autosave** checkbox. versions.title: Biter pathfinding + evolution patch
versions.notes:
"Biter pathfinding + evolution" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Biter pathfinding (grid A\*):** biters no longer beeline into whatever building blocks them. Each biter carries a waypoint path computed by `find_biter_path` in `scripts/main.gd` — a deterministic A* over the 56×56 grid where cells holding a `blocks_biters()` building are obstacles (belts, poles, splitters, and underground belts are walked over, exactly as before) and the goal cell is always enterable. The biter steers between waypoints; when it gets within attack range of its target (nearest building or the player, unchanged) it attacks as before. Paths are recomputed on spawn, when the ~2 s repath timer expires, and when the next waypoint is blocked by a building placed after the path was computed — staggered to at most **4 recomputes per tick** so a full wave cannot hitch the game; a biter that misses its recompute keeps its old path or the straight-line behaviour for that tick. **No path -> fallback:** when A* finds no route (e.g. the target is sealed inside a complete wall ring), the biter uses the original straight-line movement and chews the blocking building, so a perfect ring is a delay, not an exploit.
- **Evolution (new GameState state, 0..1, saved):** grows **+0.0002/s** with elapsed time, **+0.02** per nest destroyed (in `damage_nest`), and **+0.001** per science pack consumed by a lab (either colour). The HUD top bar shows **"Evolution: NN%"**. Effects: newly spawned biters get toughness ×(1 + evolution) in `spawn_biter` (HP, damage, and base speed scale via the existing toughness formula), `wave_size` adds `floor(evolution × 4)` on top of the base curve (up to +4), and biter movement speed scales ×(1 + 0.2 × evolution) at move time. Evolution never decreases.
- **Harness note:** the v0.1.4 underground pair at (20,10)/(23,10) sits ~9 tiles from a nest, and with the longer v0.1.5/v0.1.6 sections an ambient biter could chew through an end (80 HP) before the save round-trip — the harness now clears biters and re-places a missing end (placement re-pairs it) before saving, and asserts the pair is intact. Gameplay behaviour is unaffected; this is test housekeeping for a pre-existing exposure that the added sections happened to trip.
- **Save format:** saves gain `evolution`. v0.1.0–v0.1.5 saves still load (evolution defaults to 0).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **239/239 checks passed** (all 222 v0.1.5 checks plus 17 new: biter paths to and attacks its target building with pathing active, A* routes through a wall column's gap cell and never steps on a wall, the goal cell is enterable even when it holds a building, a fully sealed goal yields no path, spawned-biter HP scales ×1.5 at 50% evolution, wave size gains +2 at 50%, a nest kill adds exactly +0.02, a consumed science pack adds +0.001 while completing Logistics, evolution creeps with time, the top bar renders "Evolution: 42%", the underground-pair save-prep guard, and save/load preserving evolution). versions.title: Splitters + underground belts patch
versions.notes:
"Splitters + underground belts" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Splitter (new building):** hand recipe in the Buildings crafting tab — 4 iron plates + 2 iron gears, no tech gate, 1.5 s craft time. It reuses the belt's one-item buffer mechanics (`belt_item` in `scripts/building.gd`), so belts, inserters, and miner eject all feed it with no special cases, and inserters can take its buffered item back out (belts, splitters, and underground ends are one "belt-like" family for inserter source/target rules in `scripts/main.gd`). Its tick advances the item at belt speed, then delivers **round-robin — front, then left, then right relative to facing**: each delivery tries outputs starting at the round-robin pointer, the first building that can accept takes the item, and the pointer advances past it; if all three outputs are blocked the item is held. Passive — **0 power draw**, like belts. Visual: a belt-style flat base in a distinct green with raised side blocks and the travelling plate/item meshes; no working lamp (documented as not required for a passive building). The building panel shows the buffered item and the last output used.
- **Underground belt (new building, one item type for both ends):** hand recipe in Buildings — 5 iron plates + 2 iron gears, no tech gate, 2.0 s. **Pairing model (the documented simplification):** each end has a role, entrance or exit. Placing an end that lies in the front line (straight row/column, same facing) of an unpaired entrance within **4 tiles** makes it that entrance's **exit** and links the pair both ways; otherwise the new end is an **entrance**, and if an unpaired exit already sits in its own front line within 4 tiles they pair up (orphaned exits can be re-paired). An already-paired entrance is never stolen. **Flow:** the entrance accepts items like a belt; on its tick, with a linked exit and nothing in transit, the item goes underground and surfaces on the exit after **distance ÷ (1.4 × belt-speed multiplier)** seconds; the exit then outputs forwards exactly like a belt (it is part of the belt tick). If the exit is occupied when a transit completes, the item waits inside — **queue of 1 in transit per entrance** (the entrance may buffer one further item meanwhile). Deconstructing either end unlinks the pair (the survivor keeps its role, unpaired) and refunds 1 item per end as normal, plus any in-transit item. The role is shown by a marker post on the building (orange = entrance, cyan = exit) and in the building panel (role, linked cell or "unpaired", item in transit). While the underground ghost is up, a pairable hover cell shows **"Will link to underground entrance/exit (N tiles)"** in the hover readout and the ghost's secondary marker highlights the partner cell. Single placement only — drag-place stays belts/walls only (these types are excluded from the drag list, so dragging with one selected is a no-op, not a crash).
- **Both buildings:** normal `can_place` validation, rotation with R (both are directional), minimap/big-map colours (splitter green, underground belt purple), inventory-menu placement (they are not added to the number-key hotbar), building-panel support, hover readout ("Splitter - Working", "Underground Belt - Unpaired entrance (no exit)", and so on via the shared status derivation), deconstruct refunds of the building plus its buffered item, and no power draw. Biters walk past them like belts (they do not block).
- **Save format:** building records gain optional splitter fields (round-robin pointer, last output) and underground fields (role, partner cell, in-transit item and remaining time). Links are rebuilt on load and validated for mutuality, so a one-way link cannot survive a load. v0.1.0–v0.1.3 saves still load (new fields default cleanly).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **176/176 checks passed** (all 138 v0.1.3 checks unmodified, plus 38 new checks: both recipes exist in Buildings with no tech gate; splitter round-robin distribution over front/left/right acceptors including the wrap-around 4th item, hold-when-blocked, and inserter extraction; underground pairing in line within 4 tiles, no pairing at 5 tiles, transit delivery through the exit onto a belt into a chest, deconstruct-the-exit unpairs the entrance with refund, re-pairing with a fresh exit; hand-craft enqueue of both buildings; and a save/load round-trip preserving the splitter buffer and the pair's roles and links). versions.title: Audio + build QoL patch
versions.notes:
"Audio + build QoL" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Procedural event SFX (new `scripts/sfx_player.gd`, no new autoload):** main creates an `SfxPlayer` node in code — a pool of 8 AudioStreamPlayers playing AudioStreamWAV streams synthesized in code (16-bit PCM sine/square/noise bursts with envelopes, different pitch and shape per event). Events wired at their real call sites: place building, deconstruct complete (hold channel and X demolish), craft queue item finished (main now consumes the completed-output list returned by `GameState.tick_crafting`), player and turret shooting, biter hit, biter killed, research complete, wave incoming warning, victory sting, UI click (every HUD button, via the shared button factory), and error buzz (no inventory to place, miner off-patch / occupied placement, unaffordable craft queue, failed building feed, out of ammo). HARD RULE kept: event sounds only — there is no ambient or background loop of any kind (a constant ambient drone was a P0 player complaint in a sibling game).
- **Audio settings in the pause menu:** a Master volume slider (0-100, driving the SFX pool's volume and the Master bus) and a Mute checkbox. Both persist in `user://settings.cfg` (ConfigFile, section "audio"), loaded at startup and saved on change — they are NOT stored in game saves.
- **Drag-place belts and walls:** with a belt or wall ghost selected, holding left-click and moving across cells places a continuous line — each newly entered cell (plus any cells skipped between frames, interpolated along the dominant axis) that passes `can_place` and where the player still has the item is placed, consuming 1 item each. Belt facing follows the drag direction (dominant axis of the movement into the cell; last movement direction wins). The place sound is throttled to at most one per 0.06 s. A simple click still places exactly one; drag-place inherits placement's existing precedence over the deconstruct/hand-mine/shoot channels and stops cleanly when inventory runs out or the button is released.
- **Hover readout:** a dedicated HUD label above the hotbar (separate from the hint line, so transient hints are never overwritten) updated from `_update_hover`. A resource patch cell reads "<Resource> patch" (for example "Iron Ore patch"), a building cell reads "<Building Name> - <status>" reusing `building_status` (the same derivation as the building panel), and empty cells are blank — the chosen option, so the line stays out of the way on bare ground.
- **Save compatibility:** no save-format changes; v0.1.0-v0.1.2 saves still load. Audio settings live outside saves.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **138/138 checks passed** (all 114 v0.1.2 checks unmodified, plus 24 new checks: sfx player exists, all 11 named events resolve to generated AudioStreamWAV streams with length > 0, muted playback is a no-error no-op, settings round-trip at volume 0.4 + muted true, hover text for patch/furnace/empty cells, and drag-place over a 4-cell run with facing, inventory, out-of-items, and occupied-cell cases). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.3/README.md`.

versions.title: Second playtest batch
versions.notes:
Second playtest batch (twelve items from Josh's playtest of the v0.1.1 web build):

- **Hold-to-deconstruct:** with nothing selected, holding left-click on a building channels a 0.8 s deconstruction — an overhead progress bar (dark backing, orange fill, facing the camera) shows the hold; releasing, moving to another cell, selecting a ghost, or opening a panel cancels with no effect. Completion refunds the building item, any belt item, and all buffer contents (the existing `remove_building` refund). X demolish mode remains as the instant alternative. Left-click precedence is now: place > repair > deconstruct > hand-mine > shoot — clicks on buildings/patches no longer fire shots.
- **Hand mining:** holding left-click on a bare resource patch channels 0.7 s per item of that patch's resource. Patches are infinite, as they already were for miners.
- **Crafting queue (replaces instant crafting):** hand recipes have craft times; clicking a recipe consumes the cost up front and queues it (FIFO — only the front item progresses, leftover tick time carries over). The crafting panel lists the queue with a live percentage on the front row; clicking any queued row cancels it and refunds the full cost, including the in-progress item. A compact queue strip above the hotbar shows the front item and how many are queued. The queue is written into saves.
- **Inventory menu (E):** lists everything carried; building stacks are buttons that select that building for placement (click again to deselect), materials are shown with counts, research-locked buildings say what they need, and the Repair Pack row toggles repair mode.
- **Building interaction panel (E or right-click on a building):** name and cell, HP bar, a live status line derived from the building's real state (Working / Idle / No power / No fuel / Output blocked / No recipe / missing inputs), all buffer contents, machine progress for furnaces and assemblers, the current research for labs, loaded shots for turrets, and — for assemblers — the recipe picker, which now lives in this panel. Non-pausing; refreshes live.
- **Manual fueling / quick-insert:** the building panel carries Feed Coal +1/+5 for boilers and furnaces (the boiler case was the request — it is how you bootstrap power before any inserter exists), Load Ammo +1/+5 for turrets, and Insert Red Science +1/+5 for labs, all respecting the buildings' normal buffer caps.
- **Working indicator:** machines get a status lamp — green while working (state tracked from the actual simulation ticks), red when blocked (unpowered powered-machine, or a boiler without coal), grey when idle. Animated cues: the miner drill rotates while mining, and the furnace flame's emission flickers while smelting.
- **Health bars for everything:** one shared overhead bar component (visible only while damaged, fill colour runs green to red) attached to every building, every biter, every nest (which keeps its text label too), and the engineer (the HUD HP readout also remains).
- **Repair packs:** new hand-crafted item (2 iron plates + 2 copper cable, Intermediates). Selecting it in the inventory enters repair mode; holding left-click on a damaged building repairs at 40 HP/s, one pack restoring up to 100 HP with fractional credit kept across buildings. Clamps at max HP (Reinforced Walls respected for walls); a healthy building reports "already at full health" and consumes nothing.
- **Starting kit:** 10 power poles at game start (was 8).
- **Scrollable menus:** crafting and research lists, help, version log, the save-slot list, the recipe list, and the new inventory and building panels all scroll inside their fixed-size panels.
- **No more tofu-box symbols:** every pictograph/emoji was removed from the game's UI strings (the web export's font cannot draw them, so they showed as boxes with numbers). The HUD now uses plain words — "Power:", "Research:", "Nests:", "Time:", "HP:", "[locked]", "> " selection markers, "->" arrows.
- **Save compatibility:** v0.1.1 and v0.1.0 saves still load (craft queue defaults empty; building HP was already serialized in v0.1.0 and still is).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **114/114 checks passed** (all 60 v0.1.1 checks, with the instant-crafting ones rewritten against the queue, plus 54 new checks for this batch). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.2/README.md`.

versions.title: Playtest-fix patch
versions.notes:
Playtest-fix patch (from Josh's first playtest of the web build):

- **Ammo economy fixed (headline):** ammo magazines are no longer gated behind Military research — the hand-craft recipe (C → Military) and the assembler recipe both cost **2 iron plates** (down from 4) with **no tech requirement**. Military research now unlocks the Gun Turret only (tech text updated; the assembler recipe picker no longer locks ammo). The engineer's gun now fires **rounds**: 1 magazine = 10 rounds, and a magazine is only consumed when the gun runs dry — the same per-magazine yield turrets already had (was: a whole magazine per player shot, so the starting 6 magazines were 6 shots; now 60). Loaded rounds are shown in the HUD inventory panel and persist in saves.
- **Wave pacing:** first wave now arrives at **5 minutes** (was 90 s), later waves every **2 minutes** (was 90 s). Wave sizes are gradual — 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4… capped at 10 (was 3, 4, 5…) — and biter toughness scales more gently (+5% per wave, was +15%). Nest ambient spawns slowed: first spawn at 60 s, then every **40 s** (was 18 s), and only while fewer than 8 biters are alive in total (the old cap counted all biters against a 24 limit).
- **Belt items clearly visible:** the item cube on a belt is now 0.52×0.30×0.52 (was 0.34×0.22×0.34), sits on a thin dark base plate that travels with it, and its material uses **emission** in the item's colour so items pop at normal camera distances.
- **Placement preview with direction/flow:** the placement ghost is now a small rig — footprint box (green/red validity as before) plus a bright yellow-white **direction arrow** for directional buildings (belt, inserter, miner, assembler, furnace, turret), a translucent cyan **destination marker** on the front/output cell, and — for inserters — a fainter marker on the back/pickup cell. Arrow and markers track the hover cell and rotate when you press R. The pole coverage ring is unchanged.
- **Save compatibility:** v0.1.0 saves still load — `player_rounds` defaults to 0 and `wave_timer` defaults to the wave interval when the fields are absent; both are written by v0.1.1 saves.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **60/60 checks passed** (all 41 v0.1.0 checks plus 19 new ones for the four fixes). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.1/README.md`.

versions.title: Initial playable build
versions.notes:
Initial playable build — 3D grid factory automation on one flat building layer:

- 56×56 tile world; resource patches (iron ore, copper ore, coal, stone) from a fixed seed (12345) so saves regenerate them identically.
- Controllable engineer: WASD movement with a following angled camera and wheel zoom; mouse ground raycast build cursor; shooting with ammo magazines.
- Buildings (all 1×1): Miner, Conveyor Belt, Inserter, Furnace, Assembler, Chest, Lab, Boiler, Steam Engine, Power Pole, Stone Wall, Gun Turret — placement ghost with rotation (R), demolish mode (X) with refunds, hotbar (1–9/0) with research locks.
- Item flow: miners auto-eject, belts visibly carry items tile to tile, inserters move items between belts and building buffers; furnaces smelt ore→plate and stone→brick at 1 coal per smelt (burner, no power draw).
- Steam power: boilers burn coal (assumed piped — no fluid system in v0.1.0), adjacent steam engines generate, power poles project a 4.5-tile coverage radius; global satisfaction scales machine speed; HUD power readout.
- Hand crafting (C) in a clean tabbed panel — Buildings, Intermediates, Science, Military — instant crafting, locked recipes greyed with the required tech named.
- Research (T): labs consume red science packs. Techs: Automation, Military, Logistics, Power Efficiency, Reinforced Walls, with prerequisites and immediate unlocks.
- Biters and 5 destroyable nests at the map edge: nest spawns plus escalating timed waves; turrets consume ammo magazines; the player can walk out and shoot nests dead (each drops 2 red science); destroying all nests shows a victory banner and sandbox play continues. Player knockout = respawn at spawn, factory untouched.
- Minimap (live) + big map on M with drag-pan and wheel-zoom.
- Pause menu on Tab or Esc with real SceneTree pause (Tab is primary because Esc exits pointer lock in web builds), containing Help, the in-game Version Log, named save/load, and a safe Restart.
- Named save/load slots as JSON in `user://saves/` — buildings (with buffers, recipes, HP), inventory, research, player, elapsed time, and nests — plus F5 quicksave / F9 quickload.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, and a feature harness run as a scene — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.0/README.md` for the harness result and the single-threaded Web export record.

versions.title: Requested by Josh on 2026-10-08
versions.notes:

versions.title: Initial playable build
versions.notes:
Initial playable build — the full requested feature set in 2D top-down form:

- **Explore a city:** 3600×3600 procedural city (road grid, ~50 buildings, abandoned cars, park with garden), Camera2D follow.
- **Zombies + day/night:** wander/chase/attack AI, barricade chewing, 240s day cycle with night darkening, night spawns faster, zombies faster/tougher at night and scaling by day; kill counter; 35% ground-loot drops.
- **Scavenge:** loot containers with a random loot table and 45s respawn.
- **Crafting (C):** Wooden Bat, Spear, Pistol, Rifle, Bandage, Barricade Kit, Farm Plot Kit.
- **Weapons:** Fists / Bat / Spear melee (hold click; also chops trees) and Pistol / Rifle ranged with magazines, reserve ammo, and R reload.
- **Trees:** click/E chops for +1 wood per hit, +5 on felling, 60s regrow.
- **Barricades (B build mode):** ghost preview, Barricade / Reinforced / Farm Plot variants, HP, zombie damage, E repair for 1 wood.
- **Farming:** plant 1 seed → 30s growth → harvest 2–3 food + 1–2 seeds (renewable).
- **Survivors:** 6 recruitable (first free, then 1 food); orders Follow / Guard Here / Stay / Work Farm via mouse-aim + 1–4, plus G (all Follow) and J (all Guard); survivors auto-fight zombies; name/order/HP labels.
- **Healing:** Q heals self, F heals nearest recruited survivor (bandage +30, medkit +70); X eats food (+35 hunger, +5 HP); hunger drains and starving hurts.
- **Menus:** Tab/Esc pause menu with Help and an in-game Version Log; any open menu pauses the game; death screen with Restart.

Validation: Godot 4.7.2 headless — import clean, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, 28/28 feature-harness checks passed, single-threaded Web export generated and verified (`GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false`). Export record: `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival2D/v0.1.0/README.md`.

versions.title: Rename a save, Fast Inserter
versions.notes:
- Rename a save: every save in the Save and Load lists has a Rename button. Type the new name and press Enter (Esc cancels); its picture moves with it, and if it's the farm you're playing, it keeps saving under the new name.
- Fast Inserter (research it in the shop after the Long Inserter): swings more than twice as fast as an Inserter, for busy ovens, smelters and docks. Made from an Inserter, 2 gears and 2 copper plates.

versions.title: Sawdust and mulch
versions.notes:
- Crafting planks now also leaves sawdust (a weak fuel). Assemblers making planks pile it on the side, so it never ends up on the plank belt: take it by hand or with an inserter filtered to Sawdust.
- Mulch (4 sawdust make 2): put it on a garden bed and the bed stays watered for 3 harvests, through dry spells too.
- Mushroom Logs (wood and sawdust) sprout 6 mushrooms each in a dark Mushroom Cellar, which needs no power.

versions.title: F3 overlay and save sizes
versions.notes:
- F3 shows a performance overlay: how long a sim tick and a frame take, buildings, belts and belt items, machines, drones, carts, barges, bugs, the world's size, and chunks generated, so slowdowns in big factories are easy to report and find.
- The load menu shows each save's size and, at the top, how full storage is.
- When storage is nearly full (80%: the browser's own estimate on the web, otherwise 50 MB of saves), a card warns you after a save, and the load menu offers to clear old autosaves (all but the newest of each world); Export saves anything you want to keep.

versions.title: Night ambience and graphics presets
versions.notes:
- Night on green land: fireflies blink over green meadows, glowing mushrooms light up the green pines, and crickets sing, louder the more green, clean land is around you. Barren and smoggy land stays dark and silent, so you can hear the difference between restored and ruined land.
- Graphics presets in Settings: Low (no shadows, wildlife, water ripples, or swaying grass, and a lower render scale), Medium, and High.
- On first launch the game watches the frame rate for a few seconds of play and picks a preset for you (it says so if it picks Low or Medium).

versions.title: Recipe pins and drag-to-set crops
versions.notes:
- Pin a recipe to the screen: Ctrl-click it in the crafting grid (or press Pin in the item lookup). Its ingredients show at the top right with how many you have, turning green as you gather them, and the recipe says when it's ready to craft. Up to three pins; Unpin removes one.
- Drag to set crops: hold a seed and drag across Garden Beds and Farm Towers. Empty beds are planted with it and every tower you pass is set to grow that crop.

versions.title: First-day checklist, idle reasons, item lookup
versions.notes:
- First-day checklist: on a new world (not a tutorial), a small list on the left walks you through the real game in place (salvage scrap, craft and place a bed, plant wheat, sell a crop, build a burner, lay a belt), ticking off each step. Hide it for the world with its Hide button, or turn it off for new worlds in Settings.
- Why is this idle? Every working building's window starts with one plain sentence: working, no power, low power, out of fuel, no recipe, missing flour, output full, no seeds, needs feed, out of season, or too much smog. Its Show button looks up the missing item, or opens the map at the building with the power overlay on.
- Item lookup: middle-click (or Ctrl-click) an item in the inventory or the crafting grid to see every recipe that makes it and every recipe that uses it, with the machine. Click any item there to look that one up (Back returns).

versions.title: Valley journal and field notes
versions.notes:
- Valley journal: ten pages of an old diary and letters turn up, in order, while you salvage ruins and wrecks, telling why the valley dried up and what the old farm grew. Read them on the new Journal tab of the collection book (J).
- Some pages teach a lost recipe (cornbread, the tart, cheese), and one marks an overgrown greenhouse on your map.
- Field notes: a Research Desk studies samples (crops, dishes, and parts like gears and plates), one a second, by hand or inserter, earning field notes worth about a quarter of each sample's price. Shift-click a research card in the shop to pay for it in field notes instead of money (one note pays for $5), so an automated sample line feeds the tech tree without flooding the market.

versions.title: Named regions and greening ripple
versions.notes:
- The valley is split into named regions (64×64 tiles: Home Meadow where you start, then names like Dry Creek, Ashen Flats, or Old Mill Hollow), each with a restoration %: how much of its land is green. The map (M) shows their borders, names, and %, and the hover tooltip says which region you're in.
- Restoring a region (60% green) pays a reward that grows with each one, with a little scene: a ring of sparkles, a chime, and a card.
- Returning wildlife now follows the regions: birds come back when a region is a quarter green, deer when one is restored, and the white stag after three.
- Greening ripple: a soft flash and sparkle (and a faint twinkle) where a tile turns fully green near you.

versions.title: Irrigation ditches and river barges
versions.notes:
- Irrigation Ditches: with the Shovel, dig channels (lined with ditch boards, 1 plank makes 4) and drag to dig a line. A ditch joined to a lake or river, directly or through other ditches, fills with water, and the land beside it counts as watered: thirsty crops grow at full speed and dry spells don't slow them. Belts, pipes, and poles can cross ditches; hold right-click to fill one in.
- River barges (research after Cart Stations): a Barge Dock on a river bank is a crate set to Send or Receive. Put Barges in a Send dock and they float loads along the river to the nearest Receive dock on the same water. Rivers flow away from where you started: fast downstream, slow coming back.
- Hazard, with a warning card the first time you have a dock or barge: on a spring flood day barges stay moored, and a barge already out on the river when the flood comes sinks with its load. Floods are forecast the evening before.

versions.title: Reed beds and returning wildlife
versions.notes:
- Reed Beds (shop, after the Fish Trap): place one on a lake or river shore and its reeds slowly clean the smog out of the water and air around it, with no power or filters, so fish come back to polluted lakes. They green the shore too.
- Wildlife comes back as the valley greens: birds (at 1,500 green tiles), then deer (5,000), then a rare white stag (12,000). Each arrival is news and an entry on a new Wildlife page of the collection book.
- Birds fly over green land and now and then drop wild seeds where the green thins out, and wildflowers grow there: slow, free greening. Deer graze on green land, and once it's back you may spot the white stag.

**Limitations:** Wildlife milestones count green tiles across the whole valley for now.

versions.title: Seed bombs and biodiversity
versions.notes:
- Seed Bombs (2 wheat seeds and a stone make 2): hold one and click bare ground within 8 tiles to throw it. Wildflowers grow there over a couple of minutes and slowly green the land around them: weaker than a tree, but a fun way to green places you won't build on, and bees visit them.
- Seed Spreader (shop, after the Composter): fill it with seed bombs and it throws one every 20 s onto bare ground up to 6 tiles away.
- Biodiversity bonus: land greens a little more strongly where several kinds of plant grow close together (crops, trees, orchard trees, wildflowers, wild plants): +8% for each kind past the first, up to +32%. The hover tooltip names the kinds near a tile, and Alt view shows the bonus over the land.

versions.title: Fermenting Crock
versions.notes:
- New Fermenting Crock (no research, stone and planks): it needs no power or fuel but takes about half a day a batch. Cabbage becomes Sauerkraut, milk Yogurt, and grapes Vinegar.
- Ferments never spoil and sell for half again as much in winter, a cheap early alternative to the Canning Line.
- New crop: Cabbage (seeds in the shop; grows best in spring and autumn, on clay). The Diner serves sauerkraut and yogurt.

versions.title: Fibre and cloth
versions.notes:
- Two fibre crops, Flax and Cotton (seeds in the shop), that never spoil.
- New research, Fibre and cloth: the Spinning Wheel spins them into yarn and the Loom weaves Linen and Cloth.
- Cloth bags 50 wheat into a Grain Sack (hand or assembler) that ships for more than the loose wheat and doesn't push the wheat price down.
- An Apron (3 cloth) makes hand crafting 15% faster while it's in your backpack; crafting a Sun Hat (linen and cloth) lets you wear one.
- A fifth village tier, Gentry, wants linen with apple pie and cider.

versions.title: Biogas Digester
versions.notes:
- Chicken Coops and Dairy Barns now leave manure on a pile of its own (up to 20). It never mixes with the eggs or milk: take it by hand from the window, or with an inserter filtered to Manure.
- New Biogas Digester (shop, after the Chicken Coop): it rots manure, spoiled food, and spare crops into Biogas canisters. Manure gives the most gas.
- Biogas is a fuel that burns with no smog at all, so a Biomass Burner on biogas is a clean generator (it works in furnaces and other burners too).
- Hazard, with a warning card the first time you have a digester: if its canister shelf fills, the tank fills and pressure builds (a gauge in its window and tooltip), and after a minute and a half at full pressure it vents a burst of smog.

versions.title: Splitter and chest filters
versions.notes:
- Splitters have an item filter: pick an item and which side it goes, and that item only leaves on that side while everything else leaves on the other, for sorting a mixed harvest belt.
- Crates, supplier and requester chests and iceboxes have slot filters: lock a slot to one item (click a slot under the chest's stacks) and it only ever holds that item, so mixed crates stay tidy for inserters. Right-click opens a slot again.
- Both are copied by blueprints and Shift-click copy and paste.

versions.title: Belt and pipe drag helpers
versions.notes:
- Dragging a belt or pipe line through something in the way (a building, a rock, a river) tunnels under it: once the drag comes out the other side, the last piece before the obstacle becomes an underground entrance and the exit goes down past it, if you have a pair of undergrounds and it's within their reach.
- Pipes now follow the drag one tile at a time like belts, so fast drags leave no gaps.
- Ctrl+Z undoes a tunnel like any other part of the drag.

versions.title: Round belt corners
versions.notes: - Belt corners carry you round the curve, keeping your distance from the corner, instead of pushing you straight ahead: sit on a 2×2 loop of belts and you go round and round.

versions.title: Seeing the ground
versions.notes:
- Soil view: press G (or the Soil button) to see every tile's soil in strong colours, even under grass: brown loam, red clay, yellow sandy.
- Hovering a building that isn't square (like a 3×2 Boiler) now highlights only the ground under it.
- Zooming the map's live view in far from your farmer now shows the rubble, trees, plants, ore and ruins there too.
- Choking vines and overgrown greenhouses have models now (they were invisible), and show on the map in purple and cyan.
- The map's Show row has an All off / All on button, and an inserter's filters can be switched off (it moves anything) without clearing them.

versions.title: Right Alt, FPS counter, smoother inventory, time-lapse rate
versions.notes:
- Only the right Alt key toggles Alt view now (the button says so); the left Alt is free for pings.
- Settings has a Show FPS option: frames per second and the slowest recent frame, under the minimap.
- The open inventory rebuilds about five times faster and at most four times a second, and no longer rebuilds whenever money comes in, so walking with it open doesn't stutter.
- The time-lapse window lets you choose how often a snapshot is taken: 4 or 2 a day, every morning, every 2 or 3 days, or once a week.

versions.title: Belt cost, steady farmhouse window, boilers
versions.notes:
- Conveyor belts now cost an iron plate and a gear (2 belts per craft) instead of a plank and a gear.
- The farmhouse window (and other long windows) no longer flickers: it waits for its text to settle before resizing, and its scroll bar no longer comes and goes.
- Boilers: a pipe on a boiler's steam outlet used to join the water pipes, so it showed (and carried) water. Steam pipes now stay steam, and only the two end ports take water.

versions.title: A new valley
versions.notes:
- Once the Great Seed Vault opens, its window offers a new valley: a fresh world a step harder (more smog, less soaked up, ore thinner and farther apart).
- Take two perks along: a seed bank (30 of every seed you've grown), your bred strains, your recipe book, or a nest egg.
- The old world stays saved; the HUD shows which valley you're in.

**Limitations:** Solo only: in co-op, start the new valley from a solo game.

versions.title: Co-op trading and weekly goals
versions.notes:
- Co-op trading (own backpacks): stand near a friend, open your inventory, and hand them the item you're holding (one or all) or money.
- Co-op goals: once a friend has joined, each week brings a shared goal to make a dish together; when it's met everyone gets the reward. It shows under your orders.

**Limitations:** Goals count dishes made by machines.

versions.title: Tutorials for the wider world
versions.notes:
- Five new tutorials under The wider world: Biomes and far crops, The village, Breeding seeds, Keeping food fresh, and The Great Seed Vault.
- The Tutorials screen now shows its lessons in two columns.

versions.title: Money charts and the factory planner
versions.notes:
- Production window, Money tab: your balance, what you earned and spent each in-game hour, and reputation, over the last day or week. Point at it for the numbers.
- Production window, Planner tab: pick a dish and how many a minute; it lists the machines, garden beds, Farm Towers, and seeds needed, back to the crops, and what to bring in.
- Settings: the factory planner can be switched off.

**Limitations:** The planner assumes full speed (powered machines, loam, no strains). Money history starts from this version.

versions.title: Conditions, cart schedules, cargo drones, personal logistics
versions.notes:
- Conditions: wire an inserter (or a belt: Ctrl-click it) to a chest and it only runs while the chest has less or more than an amount.
- Cart schedules: give a Cart Station a list of stops; its carts go round them in order, loading or unloading and waiting until full, empty, or 30 s at each.
- Cargo drones (research): Drone Pads that send goods by air to the nearest Receive pad anywhere, no rails needed.
- Personal logistics (research): logistic drones keep chosen items stocked in your backpack and take away what you mark as trash, while you're in a roboport network.

**Limitations:** A schedule holds up to 8 stops. Conditions read one chest.

versions.title: The merchant, overgrown greenhouses, rivers
versions.notes:
- A travelling merchant visits your farmhouse every few days (announced the evening before): rare seeds, goods, a tool at 30% off, ready-made blueprints, and good prices for odd surplus, for one day only.
- Overgrown greenhouses far out in the valley: clear the choking vines, then open them for heirloom seeds (pumpkin, saffron, vanilla) found nowhere else, and new dishes from them.
- Rivers wind across the land beyond the home valley, with fords to cross. Bridges (craftable from the start) carry you, belts, pipes, rails, and poles over water; Water Wheels on a river bank make steady power.
- Orders now only ask for things you can make (no smoked fish before you have a Smokehouse).

**Limitations:** Rivers and greenhouses only appear in land explored from now on.

versions.title: Dish quality and drinks
versions.notes:
- Dish quality: dishes made from bred, in-season, or fresh ingredients come out Fine (silver star) or Excellent (gold star), selling for up to 30% more and counting for more at the fair.
- Drinks (research): tea grows wild in the cold pines and coffee in the dry hills. A Roaster makes tea and coffee; a Juicer makes juice from apples, grapes, strawberries, or blueberries.
- Villagers want a drink: juice at tier 2, tea at tier 3, coffee at tier 4. The Diner serves drinks, cider, and apple pie.

**Limitations:** Quality is one level per dish (like freshness), not per item.

versions.title: Soil types and orchards
versions.notes:
- Soil types: loam, clay, and sandy patches across the valley (more clay in the wetlands, more sand in the dry hills). Each crop grows 20% faster on its favourite soil, and fertilized harvests slowly turn poor soil into loam. Hover the ground to see it.
- The Shovel (shop): dig up soil and lay it somewhere else, under garden beds or bare ground.
- Orchards (research): Apple, Peach, and Cherry Trees take two days to grow, then fruit every season for good. A Cider Press, apple pie, and peach and cherry jam.

**Limitations:** Soil in land you'd already explored is worked out from the seed (nothing there changes otherwise).

versions.title: Fair warning, difficulty presets, creative mode
versions.notes:
- Fair warning: the first time you come near a hazard (the dry hills, lakes that flood, smog wrecks, blight nests, heavy smog, spoiling food), a card explains it so you can plan before it costs you anything.
- Grass fires now only start and spread in the dry hills, and the evening before a storm, drought, or flood you're told what's coming.
- Difficulty presets on the new-world screen: Relaxed, Normal, and Hard set the sliders and options for you.
- Creative mode (a new-world option): build for free with everything unlocked, an endless backpack, instant free crafting, and a million dollars. No achievements; saves are marked creative.
- The new-world screen fits again: the extra options moved to the right-hand column.

**Limitations:** Each hazard card shows once per world.

versions.title: Collection book, message log, save pictures
versions.notes:
- The collection book (J, or the pause menu): every crop, dish, wild find, and biome you've come across, with hints for the ones you haven't. Finishing a page wins a trophy for the farmhouse and money; the Dishes page also earns a Chef's hat and the Biomes page an Explorer's hat.
- The message log (O): scroll back through the news, events, and chat, by day and time.
- Each save in the load menu shows a picture of the farm when it was saved.

**Limitations:** Saves made before this version have no picture until you save them again. The book fills in what an older save had already sold or made.

versions.title: Village mailbox, cottage tiers, fairer freshness
versions.notes:
- The village: families' letters and cottages now arrive in your farmhouse mailbox. Take the cottage and place it wherever you like; pick it up to move it and the family moves with it.
- Cottage tiers: every cottage of a tier wants the same basket. Fed two mornings running, a cottage moves up a tier (settlers, villagers, townsfolk, merchants), wanting more and thanking you more.
- Serve-only economy (experimental new-world option): the dock doesn't buy food; families pay for what you bring them, and food given at the dock becomes reputation through the food bank.
- Freshness is fairer: each food has one freshness level for all of it, raised by new food in proportion and lowered by time. Stacks only start spoiling below 30%, a little at a time, and moving food can't refresh it. Alt view shows a freshness bar.
- Weather events (storms, droughts, floods) are now a new-world option.
- Photo mode: H hides your farmer (and friends') for the picture.

**Limitations:** Worlds made before this keep the village's old cottages; new families arrive by mail. Weather events are off in older worlds.

versions.title: Seed breeding and weather events
versions.notes:
- Seed breeding (research): a Seed Lab breeds better strains of a crop, Bountiful, Quick, or Hardy, up to level 3. Beds take on the best strain when they're planted, and bred seeds show a gold star.
- Storms (in weather worlds) can knock out wind turbines until you repair them (2 gears).
- Droughts can start grass fires that spread over green land and burn crops and saplings. Bare ground, water, roads, and sprinklers stop them; rain puts them out.
- Spring floods wash out unripe crops near the lakes.
- The forecast and the top-left weather show storms, droughts, and floods coming, and there are Fire and Turbines down alerts.

**Limitations:** You can't put a fire out yourself; plan fire breaks and sprinklers. Greenhouse crops don't use strains.

versions.title: Music, photo mode, and your farmer
versions.notes:
- New music: tracks for spring, autumn, winter (with bells), and the night, alongside the original. The music follows the season and the time of day, crossfading as they change.
- The factory sounds busier as it grows: a soft hum and clatter that rises with the machines working around you.
- Photo mode (F2, or the pause menu): the HUD hides, the camera flies free (WASD, Q/E to turn, R/F to tilt, wheel to zoom), and Space saves a picture.
- Your Farmer (pause menu): pick a hat (straw hat, cap, beanie, flower crown, or none), a shirt colour, a name tag colour, and a name. Co-op friends see them, and chat uses your name.

**Limitations:** The new music is built in the background after the game starts, so the first minute plays the original loop.

versions.title: Co-op chat, own backpacks, touch and gamepad
versions.notes:
- Co-op chat: press Enter to type a message everyone sees.
- Own backpacks and wallets (a new-world option for co-op): buildings are shared, but each player has their own backpack, money, and crafting queue, and comes back to it when they rejoin. A dock or diner pays whoever built it; village thanks are split.
- Gamepad support: the left stick walks, the right stick moves a cursor that works like the mouse, and the buttons click, rotate, open the inventory and map, switch hotbar slots, zoom, and shoot.
- Touch screens: a joystick to walk and buttons to take apart, rotate, put away, and zoom (or pinch to zoom). They appear when you touch the screen.

**Limitations:** With own backpacks, guns, armor, and research are still shared. Gamepad buttons can't be remapped yet.

versions.title: Undo, search, and accessibility
versions.notes:
- Undo (Ctrl+Z, or Cmd+Z on a Mac): takes back your last build, take-down (putting the building back with its settings), dragged line of belts or walls, or blueprint paste.
- Search (Ctrl+F): a search box in the inventory (filters the backpack and crafting), the shop (highlights matching research), and help (finds text across every tab).
- Settings: interface size (75% to 150%), smog colour on the map (red, purple for red-green colour blindness, or dark grey), and a Controls screen to change any key.
- Windows now open over the minimap and alerts.

**Limitations:** Undo covers your own last 100 actions in this session; it isn't saved. Shift, Ctrl, and Alt can't be remapped.

versions.title: The village
versions.notes:
- A village grows around your farmhouse: as your reputation rises, families move in and build cottages (up to 12).
- Each family needs a basket of food every day, delivered to its cottage by hand, belt, or inserter. The basket grows richer as the village grows, from bread and salad to cake and fish pie.
- Well-fed families thank you each morning. A well-fed village shares a family recipe at each new level, opens a market (cheaper seeds), and lends helpers in the kitchen (faster hand crafting).
- A Village hungry alert in the evening if families haven't had half their basket.

**Limitations:** Cottages go up on free land near the farmhouse; keep some space clear around it.

versions.title: Freshness, the Test Kitchen, and the county fair
versions.notes:
- Freshness (a new-world setting, off by default): fresh crops, eggs, milk, fish, and dishes slowly spoil into Spoiled Food (compost it). Keep food in a powered Icebox, smoke fish and cheese in a Smokehouse, or can tomatoes and make jam in a Canning Line. Preserved food never spoils and sells for half again as much in winter.
- The Test Kitchen (research): try two or three ingredients together. If they make a dish you haven't unlocked, you learn it for free (it goes in the recipe book); if not, the cook may give you a hint.
- The county fair: on the last day of each season (every 4th day without seasons), enter your best dish and biggest crop at the farmhouse. Win money, ribbons for the farmhouse, and rare biome seeds.
- A County fair alert reminds you on fair day.

**Limitations:** Food on belts, in carts, and inside machines doesn't spoil. Existing worlds keep freshness off.

versions.title: Biomes and fishing
versions.notes:
- Biomes: about 100 tiles out from the start the land turns to wetlands (more lakes, frogs), dry hills (more rocks), or cold pines (pine woods), each with its own soil and grass colours, on the map too.
- Six biome crops that grow wild only in their biome and at full speed only there: rice and cranberries, olives and grapes, mushrooms and blueberries. Greenhouses grow them anywhere.
- New dishes: Rice Bowls, Cranberry Sauce, Sushi, Olive Oil, Raisins, Focaccia, Mushroom Soup, Blueberry Muffins, and Mushroom Risotto (research Wetland, Hill, and Pine cooking). The Diner serves them.
- Fishing (research): Fish Traps on lake shores (fewer fish in smoggy water) and Fish Ponds that raise fish on grain. Grilled Fish and Fish Pie.
- Alt view now shows what coops, barns, hives, ponds, and traps have made.

**Limitations:** Land you've already explored keeps its old resources; biome crops and pines only appear in land explored from now on. The home valley stays meadow.

versions.title: The Great Seed Vault
versions.notes:
- The Great Seed Vault (research, $5,000): a 5×5 goal for long games. Fill it in three stages, by hand or with inserters: foundations, a seed bank, and provisions. When it's full it opens and a wave of green rolls 72 tiles out, clearing smog, rubble, ruins, and wrecks and turning blight nests into Bloom Nests.
- Copy and paste settings: Shift+right-click a building to copy its recipe, crop, filters, station mode, or chest limit, then Shift-click other buildings to paste.
- Alerts beside the minimap: no power, no fuel, no ingredients, output full, under attack, and orders due tomorrow. Click one to see it on the map. Turn them off in Settings.

**Limitations:** One vault per world. Alerts show the first building of each kind on the map.

versions.title: Smog wrecks
versions.notes:
- Smog wrecks: ruined factories and rusted cars dot the valley, trailing smoke. Their smog withers the grass and slows crops around them, so clearing them is part of bringing the valley into bloom.
- Nests don't smell wreck smog, so wrecks never bring attacks.
- Wrecks are too big to break up by hand. The Clearing Kit does it in one pull, for scrap and machine parts. Construction drones clear them too (deconstruction planner) once you have the Kit.
- A Smog wrecks slider under Landscape when making a new world. A new achievement: Scrap dealer (10 wrecks).

**Limitations:** Older worlds get wrecks only in land explored from now on.

versions.title: Farm carts and wildlife
versions.notes:
- Farm carts (research, $350): lay Cart Rails between Cart Stations, set one to Send and one to Receive, and put Farm Carts in the Send station. A cart carries up to 200 items to the nearest Receive station it can reach, unloads, and comes back. Inserters fill and empty stations like crates.
- Life returns to green land: butterflies flutter over it, rabbits hop about (and scatter when you come close), and fish jump in the lakes. They come out by day in fair weather.
- Grass sways in the wind.

**Limitations:** Carts follow the rails without crossings or signals. Each cart goes to the nearest Receive station.

versions.title: Bloom Nests and night raids
versions.notes:
- Bloom Nests: keep Blight Jelly in a tame nest's trough as well as crops, and after 2 minutes the nest blooms for good, covered in flowers. Its friendly bugs pollinate beds within 8 tiles and slowly green the land around it.
- Night raids: packs that set out after dark are half again as big.
- Lamps (1 power each, no research needed): they light the ground around them at night.
- A new tutorial, Defending the farm: turrets, walls, your gun, and taming a nest.
- Four new achievements: Pest control, Exterminator, Blight whisperer, and Flowers from blight.

versions.title: Orders and the Valley in Bloom
versions.notes:
- Villager orders: up to three on your farmhouse board ("30 bread by day 8"), shown top left. Click the house to deliver from your backpack, or run a belt and inserter into it.
- A filled order pays well over the market and earns reputation, and each point makes orders pay 5% more. Missing the day costs a point. New orders come each morning.
- Valley in Bloom: turn half the land of the valley you started in green to win. A summary screen shows your farm's story (days, food shipped, orders, smog made, nests tamed), then you keep playing.
- Two new achievements: Good neighbor (10 orders) and The valley restored.

versions.title: Animals, compost, greenhouses, and the diner
versions.notes:
- Chicken Coop ($150): hens eat wheat or corn and lay eggs. Dairy Barn ($250): cows eat wheat, corn, lettuce, or potatoes and give milk.
- New dishes: Omelette (2 eggs + a tomato, oven, $18), Cheese (2 milk, Prep Table, $14), and Cake (2 flour + 2 eggs + milk, oven, $45).
- Composter ($80): spare crops and seeds become Fertilizer. A fertilized bed grows at full speed for 3 harvests, however barren the soil.
- Greenhouse (research, powered, $500): grows a crop indoors at full speed, four beds' worth, whatever the soil, season, weather, or smog.
- Diner ($300): stock it with dishes. A customer buys one every 4 seconds, paying 15% more for each other dish on the menu, up to 75% more.

versions.title: Time-lapse
versions.notes:
- Each morning the game saves a map of your valley (on this computer, for each world).
- Time-lapse (pause menu): play the days back and watch the valley turn green, or scrub through them with the slider.
- Save GIF turns the whole time-lapse into an animated GIF to share. It downloads in the browser, or goes to your Downloads folder.

**Limitations:** Snapshots start from today, so older worlds' time-lapses begin now. Co-op friends each keep their own.

versions.title: Beehives and Air Scrubbers
versions.notes:
- Beehives (shop, $120): bees buzz around the planted beds and wild plants within 4 tiles. Beds they reach give a quarter more at harvest, and the hive fills with Honey, faster with more flowers. Bees rest in winter.
- Honey sells for $8, or makes Honey Bread ($22) and Honey Tarts ($40) at a Prep Table.
- Air Scrubbers (research, $400): a powered 2×2 machine that pulls smog out of the air within about 14 tiles, burning an Air Filter a minute. Filters come from charcoal and iron, or three from one Blight Jelly in combat worlds.

versions.title: Seasons and weather
versions.notes:
- Seasons (a New World setting, on by default; choose the season length and the season you start in). Each crop grows faster in its own seasons and slower out of them, and everything is slow in winter. Prices follow: crops out of season cost more, salads and tarts sell better in summer, and bread, pizza, and baked potatoes in winter.
- Weather (also a New World setting, on by default). Rain waters every bed (thirsty crops too) and washes smog away faster. Dry spells halve growth on beds without a sprinkler. Winter brings snow.
- A Forecast button (top left) shows the week ahead. Each morning's news says the weather and when a new season starts.
- The land shows the season: fresh in spring, warm in summer, golden in autumn, and patchy snow in winter. Rain darkens and shines the ground under grey skies.

**Limitations:** Older saves keep no seasons or weather. They're settings for new worlds.

versions.title: Blueprint library and planners
versions.notes:
- Blueprint library (L): save the blueprint in hand by name (kept across all your worlds) and take it back out any time. Copy any of them as a string to send a friend, or paste one in to import it.
- Deconstruction planner (K): drag over an area to mark buildings, rubble, rocks, trees, and ruins (a red X). Your construction drones take them away into your inventory, with what's inside. Planned ghosts there are dropped. Shift-drag unmarks.
- Upgrade planner (U): drag to mark belts, burner drills, stone furnaces, burner ovens, and assemblers (a green arrow). Drones swap each for its better version (fast belt, electric drill, electric furnace, electric oven, advanced assembler) when you have one, keeping its contents and settings. Shift-drag unmarks.

**Limitations:** The upgrade planner skips underground belts and electric drills (their better versions are a different shape).

versions.title: Production stats and map pins
versions.notes:
- Production window (P, or the new top button): every item made and used per minute over the last 5 minutes or hour, with net rates and a chart for each. Machines, drills, farms, crafting, gathering, burning fuel, and shipping all count. Esc or Tab opens the menu now (P used to).
- Map pins: right-click the map to pin a note there; right-click a pin to take it away. Pins show on the map, the minimap, and as flags in the world, and everyone in co-op sees them.
- Ping: Alt-click the world or the map to flash a ring there for everyone. Friends get told how far away it is and in which direction. Tapping Alt by itself still toggles Alt view.

versions.title: Equipment, taming, and water
versions.notes:
- Equipment bar (bottom left, like Factorio): three weapon slots and an armor slot. Guns you get fill empty slots. Click a slot to make it your active gun, or press X to switch. Hold a gun on the cursor and click a slot to equip it, or right-click to take one off. Click the armor slot to put on Modular Armor; right-click it to fit modules.
- The Pistol, Submachine Gun, and Shotgun have proper icons.
- Taming the blight: a Blight Trough (combat research) stocked with crops tames the nests within 8 tiles. Tame nests don't attack or spread, keep soaking up smog, and turn it into Blight Jelly. Sell it for $30, or make Jelly Toast (bread + jelly at a Prep Table) for $55. Each tame nest eats a crop every 15 s.
- Water has rolling waves that catch the sun, drifting light ripples, and lapping foam along the shore.

**Limitations:** Co-op farmers share the weapon slots (like the shared inventory), but each picks their own active gun.

versions.title: Landscape and clearing
versions.notes:
- New World has a Landscape section: sliders for how much Rubble, Rocks, Dead trees, and Ruins there are. The settings are in two columns now.
- Clearing Kit ($1000 in the shop, after Work Gloves): one pull on rubble, a rock, a tree, a ruin, or a wild plant takes the whole tile.
- Stone Furnaces hold 50 fuel. Stone and Electric Furnaces hold 50 ore (or stone) and 50 of what they make.
- The hover panel shows how much smog a building is making (or would make while working).
- Foresters replant where they cut a tree, and keep the ring right around them free for inserters.
- Trees you planted show deep green on the map, unlike wild plants and natural dead trees.
- Turning off Smog on the map turns it off on the minimap too.

versions.title: Smarter targets
versions.notes:
- Blight packs now go after what matters: buildings that make smog (the busiest first, idle ones too) and Gun Turrets. Lone poles, belts, pipes, crates and the like are no longer targets. They're only chewed when they're in the way.
- A nest with nothing worth attacking nearby doesn't send a pack.
- New world setting under Enemies: "Bugs attack every building", off by default, for the old behavior where anything can be a target.

versions.title: Walls and pathfinding
versions.notes:
- Blight bugs find their way: they walk around water and buildings, and when the only way in is long or there's none, they chew through the weakest spot.
- Stone Walls (combat research, 5 bricks each): 400 health and bugs can't walk through them. Drag to build a line. Bugs go around a short wall and chew through a wall that rings you in. They never attack walls for their own sake.
- A bug chasing you stops at a wall or building in its way and chews that instead.
- Attacks come from smog alone: nests soak up the smog that reaches them (taking it out of the air) and spend it on bugs, 4 smog for a bug and 20 for a brute. A nest the smog doesn't reach never attacks, however busy your base is. Nests can now be as close as 48 tiles to the start.

**Limitations:** Bugs follow the path they planned when they set out. A building put in their way later gets chewed rather than walked around.

versions.title: Combat mode
versions.notes:
- Combat mode: tick "Blight nests attack" when making a new world (it's off by default, and older saves stay peaceful). Blight nests grow out in the far valley.
- Nests smell the smog your buildings make and breathe in any that drifts over them. Enough of it and they send a pack of bugs at your smoggiest building. More smog means more and bigger attacks, and over time Blight Brutes join in. The first ten minutes are quiet.
- Bugs chew through buildings and go for farmers who come close. If they knock you out, you wake up at home. Damaged buildings mend slowly, and your house is safe.
- Gun Turrets (research) shoot bugs within 18 tiles. Load them with Magazines by hand or with an inserter.
- Guns: hold Space to shoot. You start a combat world with a Pistol and 10 Magazines. Craft Magazines (4 iron plates) and Pistols; research the Shotgun and Submachine Gun; or buy any of them in the shop's new Arms tab.
- Shoot a nest to destroy it for $50, but it sends bugs at you. Nests near your base slowly spread to new spots, away from other nests and from your buildings.
- New world sliders: Attack pressure and Nests. Smog from buildings now goes up to 5×.
- Nests show on the map, and pointing at one shows its health and how close it is to attacking. Help has a Combat page.

**Limitations:** Bugs walk straight at their target (over water and through buildings, which they chew on the way). There's no armor against bugs yet.

versions.title: Smoother co-op
versions.notes:
- Co-op is much smoother for whoever joins: their game now plays the world at a steady pace a moment behind the host, instead of jumping ahead in bursts whenever an update arrived. The host also sends far fewer messages.
- You can just squeeze between two buildings that touch.
- Belts carry you along when you stand on them.
- Limit how many slots a crate fills: click an empty slot to lock it and those after it (inserters and drones won't fill them); click a locked one to open them again.
- Belts stack 200 to a slot.
- Crafting tooltips list the raw materials a recipe comes to.
