- Help lists every crop's growth time, harvest, price, water needs, and where it grows wild.
- Smog shows as a clear red wash on the map, and buildings are drawn grey so it stands out.

versions.title: Map and looks
versions.notes:
- The map has a Show row: tick each resource (iron, copper, stone, coal, oil, water, wild plants, ...) and buildings or green land on and off.
- Zoom far into the map to see a live view of that spot from above.
- Lake shores are rounded instead of square steps.
- Crop icons are drawn properly: wheat stalks, a tomato with its leaves, potato, lettuce, strawberry, and a corn cob.
- Pipes can carry steam: connect a boiler's steam outlet to engines farther away.

**Limitations:** The live map view only shows belt items and crops near where you are.

versions.title: Fixes
versions.notes:
- Co-op: the room box sits on the left now, out of the way of building windows, and folds away with [-].
- "Someone's standing there" checks the building's real shape, so long buildings like steam engines don't block a whole square.
- Tooltips stay up while a window refreshes under the mouse (they used to switch to whatever was in the world behind).
- Greenery: each tree greens the land around it by a share that falls off with distance (10% five tiles away), and shares from several trees add up.
- Placing a building shows yellow triangles on the exact tiles where things come out, and blue ones where pipes or steam go in.
- In a crate, hold right-click on a stack and drag to take just some; they go on your cursor.

versions.title: Play at bloomworks.onrender.com
versions.notes:
- Co-op uses the server at bloomworks.onrender.com from any https page, so a copy hosted elsewhere (like itch.io) can still host and join.
- Copy invite link always gives a link friends can click to join: from another site it points to bloomworks.onrender.com.

**Limitations:** The free server sleeps when idle, so the first visit can take up to a minute.

versions.title: TURN relay
versions.notes: - Co-op can relay through a TURN server when a direct connection is blocked (phone hotspots, strict NAT, some ISPs), so more friends can join.

versions.title: Roads under buildings
versions.notes:
- Stone Roads are now paving on the ground: you can build on top of them. Hold right-click on bare road to lift it. Roads in older saves are converted.
- In co-op, construction drones leave from the farmer nearest the ghost and fly back to that farmer.
- Crafting can still take you over the backpack limit, on purpose.

versions.title: Modular armor
versions.notes:
- Modular Armor (research): wear it from the inventory and fit up to 6 modules.
- Portable Solar Panels charge it in daylight; Armor Batteries hold more charge.
- Exoskeletons make you run 40% faster each (up to two) while the armor has charge; switch them off to save power.
- A Personal Roboport lets 10 more construction drones fly at once, half again as fast.

**Limitations:** In co-op the armor is shared, like the inventory.

versions.title: Logistic drones
versions.notes:
- Roboport (research): covers 12 tiles around it, and overlapping roboports form one network. It holds up to 20 Logistic Drones and needs power for them to fly.
- Supplier Chests offer their items; Requester Chests ask for up to 3 items with amounts you set. Drones carry up to 10 at a time from suppliers to requesters in the same network, then fly home.
- Logistic Drones are made from Construction Drones and plastic.

**Limitations:** Drones fly straight to the nearest supplier with the item; they don't balance between suppliers.

versions.title: Power switches and wires
versions.notes:
- Ctrl-click a pole, then another in reach, to cut the wire between them, or put a cut wire back.
- Power Switch (research): wires to poles within 7 tiles but only joins them while its rule holds: when the batteries around it are below (or above) a level you set, always, or never.
- Use it to bring in a backup burner grid when the batteries run low at night, or to cut off less important machines when power is short.

versions.title: Oil
versions.notes:
- Oil wells: dark pools out in the far valley (never near the start), shown on the map.
- Pumpjack (research): 3×3, placed centered on a well, pumps crude oil out of the pipe connection at its front. Wells empty slowly and pump slower as they run low.
- Refinery: 3×3, takes crude oil from pipes and makes Plastic or Fuel Oil. Fuel Oil is the strongest fuel (20 MJ).
- A pipe network carries one fluid: water or crude oil. Connect a pump and a pumpjack to the same pipes and nothing flows until you separate them.
- The Advanced Assembler now takes plastic, and its research needs the Pumpjack.

**Limitations:** Older worlds only get oil in land explored from now on.

versions.title: Pick an amount
versions.notes:
- Hold right-click on a stack in your inventory and drag left or right to choose how many to hold; let go to pick them up.
- Clicking a building then puts in just that many (across clicks if it can't take them all at once).

versions.title: Construction drones
versions.notes:
- Construction Drones (research, then craft them): carry them and they fly out to ghosts within 30 tiles of you, take the building from your inventory, build it with its blueprint settings, and fly back.
- Up to 10 fly at once. Ghosts you don't have the building for wait until you do.

**Limitations:** In co-op the drones fly from whichever farmer moved last.

versions.title: Blueprints
versions.notes:
- Blueprints: press C and drag over buildings to copy them, with their recipes, filters, crops, and splitter settings. V brings back your last blueprint.
- With a blueprint in hand, click to build what you have the parts for and plan the rest as ghosts, or Shift-click to plan it all. R rotates it.
- Ghosts are see-through plans: click one to build it from your inventory (it gets the copied settings), right-click to remove it. Drones to build them for you come later.
- Export a save from the load list to a file you can send to a friend, and Import a save from a file.
- Stone Roads (from bricks): you walk half again as fast on them.

**Limitations:** Buildings can't be placed on roads; roads are their own tiles.

versions.title: Power views
versions.notes:
- Power charts show battery charge over time and what the network could make if everything ran flat out, next to what's wanted and supplied.
- Point at a chart to read its values at that moment. Click a legend entry to hide or show that line (just wind, just renewables, ...).
- "Open the full power view" in a pole or generator's window shows the charts big, across the screen.
- The map has a Power checkbox: poles, their supply areas, and the wires between them.

versions.title: Steam like Factorio
versions.notes:
- Boilers are now 3×2: water goes in at either end, from a pipe or the boiler beside it, so you can line them up. Steam comes out the middle of the front.
- Steam Engines are now 3×6 and take steam at either short end, from a boiler's front or the engine before them, so they chain too.
- Turn them with R before placing; once placed they stay put.
- Boilers and Steam Engines from older saves go back in your inventory (with their fuel) to be placed again.

**Limitations:** Steam only passes boiler to engine and engine to engine, not through pipes.

versions.title: Drills, wind, and greening
versions.notes:
- The Electric Drill is cheaper but slower. The new Advanced Electric Drill (research) is 3×3, mines the 5×5 area under and around it, and is three times as fast.
- Place an upgrade right over the building it replaces: Stone Furnace to Electric Furnace, Burner Drill to Electric Drill, Electric Drill to Advanced, Burner Oven to Electric Oven, Assembler to Advanced. It keeps the contents, recipe, and direction; the old building comes back.
- Wind turbines close together share the wind (one neighbor within 6 tiles: 2/3 each). Holding or pointing at one shows the area.
- Trees and crops add up their greening, so trees don't need gaps between them to fully green the land.
- Grass killed by smog stays dead until a crop or tree grows right beside it.
- Help lists how much smog trees, beds, and green land soak up, and how many solar panels and batteries a steady load needs.
- Shadows fade out at night, so they no longer jump at midnight.

versions.title: World settings
versions.notes:
- New World has sliders: ore richness (how much each tile holds), vein size, vein frequency, smog from buildings, and how much trees and crops soak up.
- Settings are kept with the world.

**Limitations:** Settings can't be changed once a world has started. The starting ore patches always exist, whatever the frequency.

versions.title: Assemblers
versions.notes:
- Assembler (research): a 3×3 machine that makes anything you can craft by hand with up to 3 kinds of ingredient, at half your speed. Pick its recipe from a grid of icons.
- Advanced Assembler (research): up to 4 kinds of ingredient, at 75% of your speed.
- Burner Oven: bakes everything the Electric Oven does by burning fuel, at half speed. It comes first in the research tree; the Electric Oven now needs it and the Electric Furnace.
- Charcoal: pick the Charcoal recipe in a furnace to turn 2 wood into 1 charcoal, a long-burning (10 MJ), clean fuel. Furnaces never switch to it on their own, so wood fuel stays fuel.

versions.title: Underground and fast belts
versions.notes:
- Underground Belts (research): place an entrance, then an exit up to 4 tiles further on facing the same way; items pass under whatever is between.
- Fast Belts and Fast Underground Belts (research): twice as fast, with red stripes. Lay a Fast Belt over a belt to upgrade it in place; it keeps its items and gives the old belt back.
- Underground Pipes (with the Offshore Pump): a pair facing each other up to 10 tiles apart carries water underneath. Each connects to a pipe on its back.

**Limitations:** Underground belts can't be turned once placed; pick them up and place them again. Fast inserters aren't in yet.

versions.title: Readability
versions.notes:
- Save and load rows: the save's name on top, with smaller grey details (day, date, time played, version) under it.
- Hover ore on the map to outline its whole vein in white.
- Holding or pointing at a Forester shows the square it plants and cuts trees in, and how many free tiles it has.
- Research tree: links no longer run on top of each other, and hovering a card lights up its links in gold.
- Newly planted crops show up right away, so you can tell a bed is planted.

versions.title: Inventory and crates
versions.notes:
- The inventory shows each stack in its own slot (100 of an item, 50 of a building), with as many slots as your backpack has.
- Crates hold 10 stacks: up to 1,000 of one item, or 10 different things.
- In a crate, click a stack to take it and hold it on the cursor; Shift-click to just take it.
- The put-in grid in crate and burner windows is sorted into Fuel, Ores, Materials, Crops and seeds, Food, and Buildings.
- Inserter filters: click a slot to pick from a grid of every item, by category. Right-click a slot to clear it.

**Limitations:** Older crates holding more than 10 stacks keep their items but take nothing more until they're emptied below that.

versions.title: Quality of life 3
versions.notes:
- You can walk through trees and wild plants (rubble and rocks still block you).
- Ten hotbars: Shift + a number key switches between them.
- A list in the bottom-left shows what you just picked up, fading out after a few seconds.
- Smog: the Mill makes none; Burner Drills make a lot (10/s), Stone Furnaces 5/s, Electric Furnaces 2/s.
- The dock only chimes when you sell by hand, not for every item a belt delivers.
- Alt mode icons stay put while you move and no longer cover windows.
- Hover the dock's prices to see what each item is.

versions.title: Polish
versions.notes:
- Everything you can craft, directly or by crafting its parts, gets the green frame, with how many you could make in the bottom-left. Recipes you can't make are only slightly dimmed.
- Recipe ingredients are listed in the same order everywhere.
- Garden Bed and Farm Tower seed buttons are always in the same place; seeds you don't have are greyed out.
- Drill, Smelter, and Oven are now the Electric Drill, Electric Furnace, and Electric Oven. The Electric Oven costs more.
- Building windows no longer flicker while you craft.
- Closing the inventory (E) closes the building window next to it too.
- Crate windows: Shift-click an item to put it all in, right-click to put in 5.
- Sleeping passes the night faster. "Quit to Title" is now "Save and Quit".
- Greenery speeds things up 10× less per tile, with no cap.

versions.title: Quality of life 2
versions.notes:
- Long building windows scroll instead of running off the screen. The Biomass Burner's window has one grid of fuel to click instead of a button per item.
- A new Farm Tower to start with: it tends just the beds around it, one every 5 seconds, and needs no power. The old one is now the Advanced Farm Tower, in the research tree. Older saves that have it keep it.
- Ctrl-click (Cmd-click on a Mac) a crate or machine to take everything out.
- Alt mode: press Alt (or the Alt view button) to see what's in each crate and what each machine makes.
- Drag with a power pole to lay a line of poles as far apart as their wires reach; they step back around anything in the way.
- A Quicksave button in the pause menu.
- Gears look like gears and wood looks like logs.

versions.title: Main menu
versions.notes:
- The title screen sits over a living farm and factory: wheat takes the long way to a Mill and a splitter, a belt loop carries a jumble of things in circles, drills feed smelters, turbines spin, and a sprinkler waters corn by a pond.
- The camera drifts slowly over it, and the game's buttons and bars stay hidden until you start playing.
- Leaving a game or a tutorial brings you back to it.

versions.title: Tutorials
versions.notes:
- Tutorials on the title screen: seven short lessons, each in its own practice world.
- By hand: gathering (scrap, wood, stone, ore), crafting, farming, building, and processing ore in a furnace.
- Automation: moving items with inserters and belts, and connecting a machine by copying a working example next to it.
- A panel on the left shows each step and moves on when you've done it. You can skip a step or quit, and go straight to the next lesson at the end.
- Practice worlds aren't saved and need no power.

versions.title: Water
versions.notes:
- Lakes in the valley, including a pond near the start of every world. Older worlds get lakes on empty land.
- Offshore Pumps go on the shore and push water into Pipes. Touching pipes join up.
- Sprinklers water the garden beds within 2 tiles.
- Potatoes, strawberries, and corn are thirsty: without water they take a whole day to grow. Wheat, lettuce, and tomatoes still grow fast.
- Boiler and Steam Engine: the boiler burns fuel to boil water into steam, and engines touching it make up to 300 kW each, twice as much power from fuel as a Biomass Burner.
- All of these are in the research tree, after the Smelter.
- Chimneys smoke again while their building works.

**Limitations:** Pipes only carry water (steam goes straight from a boiler to the engines touching it). Water can't be filled in.

versions.title: Research and backpacks
versions.notes:
- The shop's unlocks are now a research tree: each one needs the ones before it (Drill and Solar after the Smelter, Pylon after the Iron Pole and Battery, pizza after tomato sauce and the oven, and so on). Hover a card for details.
- Your backpack has 40 slots. Each slot holds 100 of an item, or 50 of a building. When it's full you can't gather, harvest, take things out, or pick up buildings.
- Three backpack upgrades in the research tree: +10, +10, and +20 slots.
- The inventory shows how many slots you're using.
- Picking up a splitter gives back the items inside it.

**Limitations:** Unlocks you already bought in older saves stay unlocked, even ones whose prerequisites you skipped. Crafting can still go over the limit.

versions.title: Splitters
versions.notes:
- Splitters (unlock in the shop, $120): two belts wide. One belt in becomes two belts out, split evenly, and two belts in can merge into one.
- Items keep their lane through a splitter.
- If one output backs up, everything goes to the other.
- Click a splitter to make it prefer the left or right input or output (it's even by default).
- R turns a splitter around in place. F picks up the items inside.

**Limitations:** Inserters can't take from or drop into splitters, and splitters don't filter items.

versions.title: Quality of life
versions.notes:
- A panel in the bottom-right shows what's under your cursor: contents, growth, progress, fuel, ore left, and the whole vein's total.
- The map tells you what's under the cursor too, including how much ore is in a vein.
- Inserters take up to 5 item filters, shown on a tag over them.
- Hold right-click like in Factorio: you keep working on what you started, even if the cursor moves off it.
- Right-click a recipe to craft 5. Recipes you can't make are greyed out; ones you can make have a green frame.
- Burner buildings show how much is left in the fire, and fuel items list their energy (also in Help).
- Burner drills hold 50 fuel.
- With an item on the cursor, Z drops one into the building, belt, or ground under it. F picks up items on the ground.
- Inserter arms swing and dip to grab again.
- Stone ore looks different from rocks and other ores.
- Buildings that keep their output for inserters no longer have an output chute.
- Settings have their own menu. The load list folds each world's saves away.

**Limitations:** Items on the ground aren't picked up by inserters.

versions.title: Endless world
versions.notes:
- The valley never ends: walk toward any edge and new land appears, with rubble, trees, rocks, ore patches, wild plants, and ruins with seed caches.
- New land comes from your world's seed, so the same seed always makes the same world, however you explore it.
- Older worlds keep everything and grow from their edges too.
- In co-op, whoever explores grows the world for everyone.
- The map shows everything you've explored.

**Limitations:** Rarer crops are still placed by distance from the start, so far-off land has every kind of wild plant.

versions.title: Map polish
versions.notes:
- The map (M) follows you as you walk with it open, and your dot moves live. Drag to look around; "Center on me" snaps back. It still zooms with the wheel.
- The map and minimap are sharp now: each tile is a crisp square instead of a blur.
- A Smog checkbox on the map shows or hides the smog haze.
- Crate windows: click an item to put 1 in, Shift-click for 10, right-click for all of it.
- Saves show the in-game day they were made on.

versions.title: Sound and music
versions.notes:
- Sound effects for building, taking apart, crafting, salvaging, mining, harvesting, selling, menu clicks, mistakes, and achievements.
- Birds sing now and then when you're on green land in daylight.
- A gentle music loop plays (it fades in a few seconds after the game loads).
- Pause menu: Music and Sounds volume sliders (remembered).

**Limitations:** All sounds are generated by the game itself, so they're simple for now.

versions.title: Help, commands, achievements
versions.notes:
- Help menu (H, or the Help button): basics and controls, building, farming, power and smog, money, co-op, commands, and a list of every item ID.
- Console (/ or T): /give ITEM_ID [X] gives you items (e.g. /give iron_plate 50); /help lists commands. Using a command marks the save as "commands used" for good, shown top left and on the load screen. Works in co-op.
- 16 achievements, from "First seed sown" to "Valley in bloom", each with the day and date you earned it. See them in Help, or Pause menu, then Achievements.

**Limitations:** Achievements count from this version on; earlier progress like crops planted isn't counted.

versions.title: Worlds and saves
versions.notes:
- New Game asks for a world name (a random one is suggested) and a seed: a number, any words, or blank for random. The same seed gives the same valley.
- The Load and Save screens group saves by world, showing each world's seed.
- Each world has three autosave slots that take turns, so an autosave never overwrites your most recent one. Quicksaves and exit saves are per world too.
- Pause menu: choose how often to autosave (off, 1, 2, 5, 10, or 15 minutes).

**Limitations:** Saves from before this version show under "Older saves".

versions.title: Foresters, chain crafting, fair sales
versions.notes:
- Forester (2×2): an automated tree farm. Give it saplings; it plants them on bare ground within 4 tiles, cuts grown trees for 4 wood each, and replants. Take the wood out with an inserter.
- Crafting fills in the gaps: click a recipe even if you only have the raw materials and it crafts the planks, gears, and so on it needs first. The tip says what else it'll make.
- Fixed: selling a stack at the dock by hand paid less than the price shown, because the price dropped with every item. Hand sales now pay the quoted price for the whole batch; the market price drops afterwards.
- The dock window sells 1, 10, 100, 1000, or all of an item, showing the payout before you click. Belts and inserters still sell each item at the market price as it arrives.

versions.title: Burner age
versions.notes:
- Coal: new ore patches (one near the start). Coal is the best fuel (8 MJ) but burns very dirty: 2.5× smog. Wood (0.6×) and crops (0.4×) burn clean but take farming.
- Stone Furnace (5 stone): smelts ore and stone with fuel, no power. It picks its recipe from the ore you give it (the Smelter does too now).
- Burner Inserter (1 gear + 1 plank): slower, runs on fuel, and grabs fuel for itself from what it handles when it runs low.
- Burner Drill: mines on fuel at half a Drill's speed.
- Burner buildings show their fuel and "No fuel" when empty; smog from them depends on what they burn.
- New games start with a Biomass Burner, a Stone Furnace, Burner Inserters, and more wood. Solar Panels are now a shop unlock ($150); the Biomass Burner is available from the start.

**Limitations:** Games that already have solar panels keep the solar unlock.

versions.title: Factorio rules for items
versions.notes:
- Farm Towers, Mills, Prep Tables, Ovens, and Smelters keep what they make until an inserter (or you) takes it out. They no longer push it out the front, so their facing doesn't matter. Drills still drop ore in front of them.
- Inserters drop onto belts like in Factorio: from the side onto the far lane; along the belt (with it or against it) onto the right lane.
- Fixed: an inserter without power used to grab an item and then freeze holding it. Now it waits, and shows "No power".
- Inserters dip down to grab and drop and lift as they swing.
- The Mill is a windmill: it runs on the wind with no power (faster when it's windy).
- You can't build something solid on top of yourself (or a co-op friend).

**Limitations:** Older factories that relied on machines pushing their output onto belts need inserters now.

versions.title: Trees and power charts
versions.notes:
- Fully grown trees look different: bigger, with a full dark canopy and blossoms. Young trees stay small and light green. Pointing at one says how grown it is.
- Taking apart a fully grown planted tree gives 4 wood (a young one gives the sapling back).
- Open a building, then open your inventory (E) next to it: Shift-click an item, or drag it onto the building's window, to put it in. The Farm Tower's seed buttons are gone in favor of this.
- Power windows (poles, generators, batteries) have line charts: demand vs. supply, satisfaction, and production by source (solar, wind, burners, batteries), over the last 5 s, 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, or 60 min.

**Limitations:** Chart history starts when you load the game; it isn't saved.

versions.title: Clearer menus
versions.notes:
- Hover tips now always appear to the right of what you're pointing at (or to the left near the screen edge), and show more: what it is, what it does, and how to use it.
- The crafting menu is a grid of icons grouped into Materials, Logistics, Farming, Seeds, Processing, Electricity, and Home. Hover a recipe for its name, crafting time, and ingredients (with how many you have); faded icons are ones you can't afford yet.
- Fixed: scrolling past the end of the crafting list (or any menu) no longer zooms the camera.
- Fixed: machine recipes showed little boxes with numbers (an arrow the font couldn't draw). They now read "1 Dough from 2 Flour".
- Power poles no longer block walking.

versions.title: Building comfort
versions.notes:
- Hold right-click to take a building apart (a short moment, quicker for belts), so a stray click no longer removes things.
- Placing an inserter shows a big yellow arrow on the inserter's own tile, drawn over everything, so the building it feeds can't hide it.
- Your hotbar is yours: 10 slots (keys 1–0). Drag buildings or items onto it from the inventory, drag slots to swap them, right-click to empty one. Item slots put the item on your cursor. Newly unlocked buildings fill an empty slot. The layout is remembered.
- Crate windows have a "Put in from your inventory" grid (click: all of that item, Shift-click: 10), handy for loading crates for inserters.
- Farm Tower (and Drill) windows call their output "Products (ready to be grabbed)".

versions.title: Saves
versions.notes:
- F5 quicksaves into its own Quicksave slot; F9 loads it.
- Leaving a game saves it automatically into an "Exit save" slot: quitting to the title, starting a new game, closing the window, or closing or hiding the browser tab. Continue picks it up.
- Quicksaves, autosaves, and exit saves no longer rename your game.
- The Load list can be sorted newest first or by name.

versions.title: Map, minimap, and power info
versions.notes:
- The map (M) now scrolls (drag) and zooms (mouse wheel), and shows co-op farmers too.
- A minimap in the top-right corner shows the land around you. N hides or shows it.
- Click a power pole (or any generator or battery) to see its whole network: power supplied vs. wanted, how satisfied it is, what each kind of generator is making, battery charge, and how many machines are working.
- Holding a pole shows green wires to every pole it would link to, and says how many.

versions.title: Co-op
versions.notes:
- Play together in the browser: open the pause menu and choose Host Co-op, then share the room code or the invite link. Friends type the code on the title screen (or just open the link).
- Everything is shared: the farm, buildings, inventory, crafting queue, money, unlocks, and the explored map. Each player has their own farmer, shown with a name tag and a colored ring.
- Sleeping speeds up time once everyone is asleep.
- The game never pauses in co-op. Only the host autosaves; anyone can save a copy.

**Limitations:** Co-op needs the web version and the signaling server (see README). The host's browser tab must stay visible, and very strict networks may need a TURN server.

versions.title: Ready for multiplayer
versions.notes:
- Behind the scenes: everything you do (build, remove, craft, salvage, set recipes, buy) is now a command applied between game ticks. Two copies of the game given the same commands stay exactly in step, which is what co-op will use.
- The game can snapshot its exact state and check that two copies match.

**Limitations:** No visible changes yet; co-op comes next.

versions.title: Big factories
versions.notes:
- Large factories run much more smoothly. Belts, beds, poles, panels, and other simple buildings are drawn in batches (a 3,400-building test factory went from about 2,600 draw calls to 370).
- Items on belts and crops are only drawn near the camera.
- Belts that are backed up stop costing anything until they can move again.
- If the factory ever gets too big for your computer, the game slows down a little instead of freezing.

versions.title: Pollution
versions.notes:
- Working machines put out smog: Biomass Burners the most, then Smelters and Drills, Ovens, Mills, and a little from Prep Tables. Chimneys puff smoke while they work.
- Smog drifts to nearby land and slowly fades. Green tiles, planted beds, and trees soak it up.
- Thick smog turns the ground grey, withers grass (shrinking your greenery bonus), and slows crops.
- New: Tree Saplings (2 wood). They grow into trees in 90 s; trees green the land around them and soak up a lot of smog.
- The air where you stand is shown top left; machine windows say how much smog they make; the map shows smog as grey haze.

versions.title: Bloomworks and inserters
versions.notes:
- The game has a name: Bloomworks. Your saves carry over.
- Inserters: an arm that takes items from the tile behind it and swings them to the tile in front (the arrow). It works with belts, crates, machines, Farm Towers, burners, and docks, and only picks up what the target can use right now.
- Click an inserter to give it a filter (one item only). Long Inserters (shop, $80) reach two tiles each way.
- Inserters use a little power (8 kW, 12 for long ones) while they move. You start with 4.

versions.title: Exploration
versions.notes:
- New games have a much bigger valley (160×160), covered in fog until you walk near it. You can only build on land you've seen.
- Ruined farmsteads out in the valley: rich piles of salvage that sometimes turn up gears and plates, around an old seed cache with seeds and money inside.
- M (or the Map button) opens a map of what you've explored: green land, ore, caches, your buildings, and you.
- New Tools tab in the Shop: Work Gloves (salvage twice as fast), Pickaxe (mine ore three times as fast), Trail Boots (walk 40% faster), Lantern (see farther).
- Building icons are now little pictures of the buildings themselves.

**Limitations:** Older saves keep their smaller map, fully revealed.

versions.title: Sleep
versions.notes:
- You start with a Farmhouse just north of the clearing (more can be crafted).
- From evening on, press Z near your house (or click it) to sleep: time runs 12× faster while your farm keeps working, and you wake at sunrise. Any key wakes you early.

versions.title: Market supply and demand
versions.notes:
- Every item you ship lowers that item's price a little (down to a quarter); prices recover over a few minutes. Shipping a mix pays better than flooding one thing.
- Each morning brings market news: one item is wanted (its price climbs toward double) and one is in glut (it sinks toward 60%).
- The Shop's new Market tab shows every price, whether it's rising or falling, and a chart of the last few minutes.

versions.title: Shipping, money, and progression
versions.notes:
- Shipping Dock (2×2): belt crops and food into it to sell them. Cooked food is worth far more than raw crops (a pizza sells for $28, wheat for $1). You start with one and $30.
- The Shop (B, or the button at the top): buy seed packs, unlock recipes (sauce, salad, cornbread, tart, pizza, and more) and machinery (Smelter, Drill, Oven, Iron Pole, Wind Turbine, Biomass Burner, Battery, Pylon).
- Locked recipes show in machine windows as "locked (shop)"; locked buildings stay off the hotbar and out of crafting until you unlock them.
- Click the dock to see current prices and sell straight from your inventory.

**Limitations:** Saves from earlier versions have everything unlocked.

versions.title: Power
versions.notes:
- Day and night: a day lasts 8 minutes. Nights are darker but still easy to see.
- Farm Towers, Mills, Prep Tables, Ovens, Smelters, and Drills now need electricity. Without enough they slow down; with none they stop and show "No power".
- Generators: Solar Panels (60 kW in full sun), Wind Turbines (up to 40 kW, day and night), Biomass Burners (120 kW from wood, planks, crops, or seeds when the others fall short), and Batteries (store 6 MJ for the night).
- Poles: Wooden Poles (7-tile reach, power a 5×5 area), Iron Poles (10 tiles, 7×7), Pylons (28 tiles for long runs). Holding or pointing at a pole shows the area it powers; wires hang between linked poles.
- Click any powered building to see its network: power used, wanted, and battery charge.
- New games start with a Solar Panel, a Battery, and 4 Wooden Poles.

**Limitations:** Older saves keep working, but their machines need poles and power.

versions.title: Mining
versions.notes:
- Ore patches: iron, copper, and stone. There's one of each 13–18 tiles from the start, and bigger ones farther out.
- Hold right-click on bare ore to mine it by hand (1 s each).
- Drill (2×2): place it on a patch to mine the ore under it and send it out the front.
- Smelter (2×2): iron ore to iron plate, copper ore to copper plate, 2 stone to brick, 3 scrap to iron plate.
- Gears are made from iron plates (or from scrap, as before). Ovens now take bricks and iron plates.

**Limitations:** Copper plates are for power, coming next.

versions.title: Different plants
versions.notes:
- Five new crops: tomato, potato, lettuce, strawberry, and corn, each with its own look, grow time, and harvest.
- Wild plants grow out in the valley (rarer ones farther from the start). Hold right-click on one to gather its seeds. Any crop can also be crafted into 2 seeds.
- Farm Towers can be set to one crop or "any seeds".
- New recipes: cornmeal (Mill); tomato sauce, salad, raw pizza (Prep Table); baked potato, cornbread, pizza, strawberry tart (Oven).

versions.title: Named saves and loads
versions.notes:
- Save your game under any name from the pause menu, overwrite an old save, or load and delete saves (delete asks twice).
- F5 quick-saves under the current name. The game autosaves every 5 minutes.
- The title screen has Continue (your latest save) and Load Game.

versions.title: Processing machines
versions.notes:
- Mill (2×2): wheat into flour. Prep Table (1×1): flour into dough. Oven (2×2): dough into bread.
- Machines take ingredients from belts pointing into any side and push results out the front: onto a belt, into a crate, or straight into the next machine.
- Click a machine to pick its recipe, add ingredients from your inventory, watch progress, and take output.
- Machines run faster with the greenery bonus. The Mill's sails turn and the Oven glows while they work.

versions.title: Automated farming and greening
versions.notes:
- Garden Beds: plant seeds by hand (hold seeds and click), click a ripe bed to harvest. Each harvest gives crops and the seed back.
- Farm Tower (2×2): give it seeds and it plants every garden bed within 3 tiles, harvests when ripe, replants, and sends crops out the front onto a belt or into a crate.
- Plants bring the land back: tiles around planted beds turn green, and green spreads a fading halo to its neighbors. Dead trees on green ground come back to life.
- Greenery bonus: every green tile speeds up plants and machines, up to +100% at 1,500 tiles. It's shown top left.
- Wheat seeds can be crafted from wheat. You start with a Farm Tower, 12 beds, and 12 seeds.

**Limitations:** Wheat has no use yet besides more wheat.

versions.title: Conveyor belts
versions.notes:
- Belts carry items on two lanes, side by side. Items keep their lane from belt to belt and around curves.
- A belt pointing into the side of another puts its items on that belt's near lane.
- Belts feed whatever they point at: a crate fills up (400 items) and a full one backs the line up.
- Click an item in the inventory to hold it, then click a belt to drop one on the lane you clicked (Shift for more), or a crate to put it in.
- Click a crate to see inside and take things out. F picks up everything on the belt under the cursor.

**Limitations:** Nothing produces items onto belts yet except you.

versions.title: Inventory and hand crafting
versions.notes:
- Hold right-click on rubble, dead trees, and rocks within reach to salvage scrap, wood, and stone.
- E opens the inventory and crafting. Recipes take time; Shift-click crafts five.
- The craft queue runs down the left side of the screen. Click an entry to cancel it and get the ingredients back.
- Buildings now cost items: you start with 10 belts and 2 crates. Removing a building gives it back.

**Limitations:** Belts still don't carry anything.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- A dried-out valley full of rubble, dead trees, and rocks, with a clearing in the middle.
- Walk the farmer with WASD or the arrow keys; scroll to zoom.
- Pick a building from the bar (1-9), see a preview where it would go (green fits, red doesn't), press R to turn it, click to place. Drag to lay belts in a line.
- Right-click removes a building. Q empties your hand, or picks up the building under the cursor.

**Limitations:** Belts don't carry anything yet and buildings are free.

versions.title: TURN relay and joining spinner
versions.notes:
- Players on strict networks (phone data, some campus or work Wi-Fi) can now connect through a TURN relay when a direct link is blocked.
- A spinner shows while hosting or joining, with a Cancel button; Host and Join are disabled until it finishes.
- The connection timeout message now reminds you to keep the host's tab visible.

**Limitations:** TURN credentials are built into the game, so anyone can read them. Relayed connections add some latency.

versions.title: Names and custom room codes
versions.notes:
- Pick a name in the lobby; it shows above your player and in the HUD player list, and is remembered next time.
- The host can choose the room code (2-12 letters or numbers), or leave it blank for a random one.

**Limitations:** Custom room codes need the updated signaling server; an older server ignores the choice and hands out a random code.

versions.title: First release
versions.notes:
- Top-down co-op against waves of zombies for up to 8 players, in the browser.
- Host a room for a 4-letter code or an invite link; friends join over WebRTC (peer to peer).
- Signaling runs on Render (godotwebrtc.onrender.com) for https builds.
- Press I to toggle smoothing of other players and zombies.

**Limitations:** STUN only (no TURN), so strict NAT/CGNAT may not connect. The host's tab must stay visible. No rejoin after a refresh.

versions.title: Rival geese
versions.notes:
- Rival geese in the Suburb Cul-de-sac: about 5 minutes in, one or two Canada geese with backpacks waddle in far from you. A honk in the distance and a banner warn you.
- They raid containers (emptying them), then head for the nearest exit and leave with their haul. With a minute left, they leave anyway.
- They shoot back ("Mine!"), but bonk one and its whole bag spills out.

**Limitations:** Rival geese don't fight the gnomes or raccoons, and they don't pay for exits.

versions.title: The Park Ranger
versions.notes:
- The Park Ranger: a big bear in a ranger hat who patrols one Picnic Park raid in four. A whistle and a banner warn you when he's on duty.
- He sees far, but only along his flashlight beam, which shows on the grass even when he's out of sight. Honks only dizzy him half as long.
- His Net Launcher tangles the goose for 2 seconds: no waddling, no rolling. Roll before it lands and it misses.
- Bonk him for the Ranger's Keyring (opens both locked rooms, and isn't used up) and a pocketful of good loot.

versions.title: Critter barks
versions.notes:
- Critters speak their minds: "Huh?" when a noise or a hit makes them suspicious, "Goose!" when they spot you, and "Where'd it go?" when they lose you.
- Barks float over critters you can see, so you can tell at a glance who's hunting you. Hidden critters keep quiet.

versions.title: Pigeons
versions.notes:
- Pigeons! Flocks peck along the paths. Walk past and they ignore you, but sprint, roll, shoot, or honk nearby and they burst into the air, and every critter within 20 m comes to see why.
- The first flock you get near comes with a hint: walk past them.

versions.title: Sprinklers
versions.notes:
- Sprinklers in the Picnic Meadow and on the suburb's lawns: about every two minutes they tick and hiss for 3 seconds, then spray for 12.
- Get caught in the spray and you're soaked for a few seconds: slower, and your footsteps squelch loud enough for nearby critters to hear. Critters in the spray slow down too.
- The first time one is near, the HUD explains them.

versions.title: Locked rooms
versions.notes:
- Locked rooms: the Snack Shack's Back Room and the Restrooms' Staff Closet. Find the Shack Key or the Closet Key (in bins, on the ground, on gnomes and raccoons) and press E at the door to unlock it.
- Inside each is a Supply Crate with a better roll. Keys are used up, and the doors lock again every raid.
- The Restrooms' partition now leaves a gap, so the west side (and its bin) can be reached.
- Rolled Newspapers turn up in trash bins now, as promised.

versions.title: Raid modifiers
versions.notes:
- Raid modifiers: half the time the next raid rolls a condition, shown on the Raid button before you go. Extract for a crumb bonus.
- Rainy Day (+40): rain and puddles that slow everyone, and footsteps that squelch loud enough for nearby critters to hear.
- Fireworks Night (+60): it's dark, but every firework lights up the critters around you for a moment, even behind walls.
- Big Sale (+30): more loot in containers and on the ground, and more raccoons after it.

versions.title: Paid exits
versions.notes:
- Paid exits: some raids, an exit wants something to let you through. The Ice Cream Van wants 150 crumbs' worth of loot, the Duck Boat a Car Battery, and in the suburb the Storm Drain wants 100 crumbs' worth and the Back Alley Gate some Car Keys.
- The price is on the exit's sign, in the exit list, on the map, and in the opening banner. Payment comes out of your backpack as you leave, cheapest loot first.

versions.title: The Golden Picnic
versions.notes:
- The Golden Picnic: with 3 minutes left, a golden box parachutes into the map (banner, and a gold square on the minimap and map). It's packed with 5 to 7 rare things.
- Only the few critters close to where it lands (the 3 nearest within 30 m) come to look, so the rest of the map isn't left empty.

versions.title: Music
versions.notes:
- Music! All of it made in code like the sounds: a cosy plucky loop on the title and in the Nest, a calm park tune in raids, and a tense beat with drums whenever a critter is fighting you.
- Music: On/Off on the title screen and in the pause menu, separate from Sound, and remembered.

versions.title: Import and export saves
versions.notes:
- Save Data on the title screen: copy your save as a text code (or download it as a file in the browser) to back it up or move it to another computer.
- Paste a code (or load a file) to bring a save back. It shows what you'd be replacing and asks before it does.

versions.title: Melee weapons
versions.notes:
- Melee weapons that need no ammo: the Rolled Newspaper (quick swats), the Baguette Bat (long reach), and the Frying Pan (slow, huge BONG that dizzies what it hits).
- A swing hits every critter in an arc in front of the goose, and it's quiet: only critters close by hear it.
- Find them in crates (and newspapers in bins), or buy them in the Nest. They swish and bong.
- Fixed: weapons you found and carried out in your backpack now go in the stash (they used to vanish).

versions.title: View cone
versions.notes:
- A view cone: everything outside a 110-degree cone toward the cursor (and beyond how far you can see) is darkened, with a small bright circle around the goose.
- Critters outside your cone are hidden, just like ones behind walls. Turn to look! They can still hear you.

versions.title: Bigger stash
versions.notes:
- The stash has a size now: 40 slots to start, one per stack (125 Foam Darts take 3). The Stash column shows how full it is, and each item says how many slots it takes.
- Bigger stashes in the Nest's shop: 60 slots for 500 crumbs, 90 for 1500, and 130 for 4000.
- Extracting always banks everything, even past the limit, but an overflowing stash has to be sold down (or upgraded) before the next raid.

versions.title: Sharper maps
versions.notes:
- Sharper maps: the map screen (M) and the minimap are drawn at 4 and 3 pixels per meter instead of 1, so they're no longer stretched and blurry.
- Walls, hedges, cars, and the pond get a dark outline on the map, so shapes read at a glance.
- Area names on the map step aside for nearby exit labels instead of overlapping them.

versions.title: The Suburb Cul-de-sac
versions.notes:
- A second map, the Suburb Cul-de-sac: a turning circle, The Big House you can walk into, a garage, a paddling pool behind a fence, a veggie patch, a playhouse garden, front lawns, a back alley, and a tree house.
- Its own exits: the Mail Truck where you arrive, plus two of the Storm Drain, the Back Alley Gate, the Cat Flap, and the Tree House Rope.
- A map picker in the Nest. The suburb unlocks after 3 extractions from Picnic Park (old saves count the extractions they already have).
- The Nest's Bringing column is more compact (weapons and the secure pouch side by side), and Repack moved up next to the Lost Gosling button.

versions.title: Lost Gosling runs
versions.notes:
- Lost Gosling runs: a free raid from the Nest with a random cheap kit (a Foam Blaster or Pea Shooter, some ammo, a snack or two). Nothing from the Nest comes along, so nothing is at risk.
- Extract and the haul (and the kit's weapon) goes in the stash. Get bonked and you lose only the free kit.
- One every 20 minutes; the button counts down, and the wait is remembered.

versions.title: Secure pouch
versions.notes:
- A secure pouch: two small slots (1 kg) that always come home, even if you're bonked, locked in, or give up.
- Pack it in the Nest with To pouch, or move things in and out of it from the backpack screen (Tab) during a raid.
- Bigger pouches in the Nest's shop: 3 slots and 2 kg for 400 crumbs, then 4 slots and 3 kg for 1000.
- The results screen shows what the pouch saved.

versions.title: Polish
versions.notes:
- Sound! All of it made from scratch in code: honks, squawks when you're hit, foam dart pffs, pea pops, balloon splashes, slingshot thwips, a cartoon boing when a critter goes down, rummaging, loot bloops, reloads, munching, footsteps, a happy chime when you extract, and a sad wah-wah when you don't.
- Sound On/Off on the title screen and in the pause menu (remembered).
- A minimap in the top right, turned like the camera, with the open exits (far ones pinned to the edge pointing the way).
- You can only see critters that are in your line of sight: walls, hedges, cars, and bushes hide them (and you). Hide in a bush!
- The camera shakes when you get hit or honk, and the Nest jingles when you buy and sell.

versions.title: The Nest
versions.notes:
- Enter the Nest from the title screen: your stash on the left, what you're bringing in the middle, the shop on the right. Click anything to see it and what you can do with it.
- Sell loot for breadcrumbs (or sell all junk and valuables at once). Buy weapons, ammo packs, and snacks; buying costs twice what selling pays.
- Pack your raid: two weapon slots (slot 1 starts in hand) and the backpack. Weapons start the raid loaded from the ammo you pack.
- Bigger backpacks: 16 slots and 25 kg for 300 crumbs, then 20 slots and 30 kg for 800.
- Whatever you bring is at risk. Extract and it all comes home (weapons straight back to their slots); get bonked, locked in, or give up and it stays in the park. Repack copies last raid's backpack from the stash.
- A new save starts with 100 crumbs and a Foam Blaster kit. Broke with no weapon? Mom Goose slips you a spare.
- The pause menu's Quit is now Give Up, which costs your backpack.

versions.title: Combat
versions.notes:
- The park fights back. Garden Gnomes guard spots with slingshots; Raccoons roam the park with acorn poppers, strafe, and more of them wander in as the day goes on.
- They notice you when you're in front of them and in sight (walls and hedges hide you), hear your shots, and come looking where they last saw you.
- You start each raid with a Foam Blaster and 36 darts. Click to shoot (hold for the blaster), R to reload, 1/2 or the mouse wheel to switch.
- Find the Pea Shooter (six peas per shot) and the Balloon Lobber (arcs over cover and splashes) in crates and on raccoons, plus ammo all over. Equip them from the backpack.
- Space dodge rolls through shots (costs puff). Q honks: stuns everything in front of you, alerts everything nearby, then needs to recharge.
- 100 health. H eats the snack that best fits how hurt you are (or use Eat in the backpack); food now heals.
- Bonked critters fall over and drop loot. Get bonked yourself and you lose your backpack and weapons.

**Limitations:** Every raid starts with the same free kit until the Nest arrives.

versions.title: Getting out
versions.notes:
- The park closes in 10 minutes. The clock is in the top right, and the sun sets as closing time nears.
- Ways out: the Bus Stop where you came in is always open, plus two of the Duck Boat, the Ice Cream Van, the Drain Pipe, and the Hole in the Fence, different each raid.
- Open exits glow green with a light column and a sign. Stand in one for 5 seconds to extract; stepping out cancels. The HUD lists each open exit and how far it is.
- M opens a map of the park, turned to match your view, showing the areas, the open exits, and where you are.
- Extract and everything in your backpack goes to your stash, saved between visits. Still in the park when it closes? The ranger confiscates your backpack.
- A results screen shows what you brought out (or lost) and your stash; the title screen shows the stash too.

**Limitations:** The stash can't be opened or spent yet: that's the Nest, coming later.

versions.title: Grabbing loot
versions.notes:
- Loose loot lies all over the park: walk up to anything bobbing on the grass and press E to grab it. Uncommon and better items glow with a beam in their rarity color.
- Tab opens your backpack: click an item to read about it, then Drop it (or Drop One from a stack) at your feet. Dropped things stay on the ground to grab again.
- Heavy new finds: Lawn Flamingo, Bowling Ball, Watermelon, Garden Gnome, and the very valuable, very heavy Car Battery.
- The backpack has a 20 kg limit. Go over it and you waddle slower (down to 60% at 30 kg, a crawl beyond) and can't sprint. The HUD warns you when you're too heavy.
- If your backpack is full, you only pick up what fits.

**Limitations:** Loot still doesn't leave the park: extraction is next.

versions.title: Looting chests
versions.notes:
- Picnic baskets, coolers, trash bins, and supply crates all over the park, each with its own kind of loot. Every raid rolls fresh contents.
- Walk up to one (it gets a glowing ring) and press E to search. Items turn up one at a time; rare things take longer to find, so keep the panel open.
- Click an item to move it into your backpack, or Take All. Click a backpack item to put it back.
- 26 items to find, from Bottle Caps and Soggy Fries to Gold Rings and the legendary Golden Bread. Hover for a description, weight, and worth in breadcrumbs.
- The backpack holds 12 slots; stackable things stack. The HUD shows what you're carrying and a feed of what you just grabbed.

**Limitations:** Loot doesn't leave the park yet: extraction comes in a later release.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- You are a goose in a tiny tactical helmet. Press Raid on the title screen to waddle into Picnic Park from the bus stop.
- WASD waddles (up is up on the screen), the goose faces your cursor, and Shift sprints until you run out of puff.
- Picnic Park: a duck pond, the Snack Shack, restrooms, a parking lot, a playground, a picnic meadow, and a fountain plaza, all hemmed in by hedges.
- The camera follows from an isometric angle and leans toward the cursor. Walls, trees, and cars in front of the goose turn see-through.
- The HUD shows which part of the park you're in.

**Limitations:** Nothing to loot or shoot yet: this release is the park and the goose.

versions.title: Co-op
versions.notes:
- Fight the waves together in the browser: during a run, Pause > Host Co-op opens a room and copies an invite link. Friends open the link, or type the room code under Join Co-op on the title screen.
- Everyone brings their own loadout. Friends' mechs wear their own trim color with a name and armor tag, and you see their shots.
- The robots go after whoever is nearest. Kills, the score, and repair kits are shared.
- If you go down, the run goes on: you're back up at half armor when the wave is cleared. The run ends when everyone is down, and the host can redeploy the whole team.
- Pausing in co-op doesn't stop the fight; your mech just stands still.

**Limitations:** Co-op needs the web build. The host's tab must stay visible, or the fight slows for everyone.

versions.title: Flamethrower
versions.notes:
- Flamethrower: hold its button to pour a short cone of fire. No ammo, but it runs warm.
- Anything caught in the flames burns for three seconds, taking damage the whole time; more fire keeps it burning.
- Its reticle is a translucent cone on the floor showing exactly what it will reach. Cover blocks the flames.
- Drones burn easily; tank armor shrugs off some of the heat. Enemy mechs may carry flamethrowers from wave 7.

versions.title: Plasma weapons
versions.notes:
- Plasma Gun: slow glowing bolts that burst on impact, splashing anything nearby.
- Plasma Cannon: hold its button to charge, release to fire. A full charge hits four times as hard and bursts wider; the reticle and weapon list show the charge.
- Plasma Mortar: lobs plasma over cover. Its reticle is a circle on the floor showing where it lands and how wide it bursts, with a dotted arc.
- Plasma uses cells and a little heat, and melts tank armor for extra damage.
- Enemy mechs start carrying plasma from wave 5. The hangar shows splash and charge details.

versions.title: Energy weapons
versions.notes:
- Three energy weapons, no ammo needed: Beam Laser (a continuous beam while held), Pulse Laser (rapid instant pulses), and Lance (a long-range energy spear).
- Heat: energy weapons warm your mech. Max it out and they lock until it cools; kinetic weapons keep working.
- A heat gauge sits under the reticle and under your armor bar, and flashes OVERHEATED when locked.
- Each energy weapon has its own reticle shape, and the hangar shows damage, heat, and range for every weapon.
- Drones take extra energy damage; enemy mechs resist it a little and start carrying lasers from wave 4.

versions.title: Loadouts and weapon groups
versions.notes:
- Three chassis: Scout (2 hardpoints, fast), Warden (arms plus a shoulder), and Juggernaut (all four hardpoints, slow and tough).
- Hangar (title screen, or H between waves and in training): pick a chassis, put a weapon on each hardpoint or leave it empty, and put each hardpoint in weapon group 1 to 4. A turning preview shows your mech.
- Each weapon group fires on its own button. Settings lets you choose them: click a group, then press any key or mouse button (defaults: left click, right click, Space, F).
- Lasers, reticle arcs, and the weapon list are colored by group and show the button that fires each weapon.
- Your loadout and settings are saved. Settings also has a volume slider.
- Enemy mechs come in Scout and Warden frames, and Juggernauts from wave 6.

**Limitations:** Q / E arm swapping is gone; use the hangar.

versions.title: Enemies
versions.notes:
- The machines fight back. Deploy starts waves of robots that warp in at the arena edges; each wave is bigger than the last.
- Drones: fast fliers that circle above the cover and peck with slow red bolts you can sidestep. Weak to energy weapons.
- Tanks (from wave 2): slow and armored, they path around cover, paint you with a red sight line, then fire a heavy shell. Armor blunts kinetic hits.
- Enemy mechs (from wave 3): the same mech as yours with a robot pilot and random arm weapons. They strafe and fire in bursts.
- Your mech can be destroyed: game over shows your wave, kills, and score, with Redeploy.
- Destroyed robots sometimes drop green repair kits.
- Training on the title screen keeps the old practice dummies with nothing shooting back.
- Damage numbers: red on you, gray when armor resists, yellow on a weakness. Red markers at the screen edge point to robots out of view.

versions.title: Kinetic weapons
versions.notes:
- Four kinetic weapons: Autocannon, Machine Gun, Scattergun (nine pellets), and Railgun (instant, pierces up to three targets).
- Left click fires the left arm, right click the right arm. Weapons have magazines and reload on their own when empty, or press R.
- Q and E swap the left and right arm weapons.
- Each weapon's reticle takes its shape: the arc widens with spread, the rail is a needle, and it fills back up as you reload.
- Aiming lasers end at each weapon's range.
- Tracers, muzzle flashes, sparks, damage numbers, recoil, camera kick, and synthesized gun sounds.
- Dummies take damage, break, and rebuild.

**Limitations:** Nothing shoots back yet: enemies arrive next update.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- Pilot a mech around a walled arena: the legs walk where you steer (WASD) and the torso turns to face the cursor.
- Aiming lasers run from each arm along the way it would fire, stopping at the first wall or target, so you can see what your shot would hit.
- The weapon reticle follows where the torso is actually pointing and meets the cursor once the torso catches up.
- Practice dummies stand around the arena to aim at.
- Title screen, pause menu (Esc), and this Version Log.

**Limitations:** No weapons yet: they arrive next update.

versions.title: Self-directed iteration run
versions.notes:
Self-directed iteration run, version 2 of the roadmap (per Josh's 2026-10-14 mandate) - enemies arrive; the sandbox is no longer peaceful:

- **Biter nests:** 5 nests at deterministic map-edge cells (200 HP, health bars), each spawning a biter every 30 s (max 10 alive); waves every 2 min after a first wave at 5 min, size min(2 + wave, 10), HP scaling +10 percent per wave (all first-guess balance).
- **Biters:** seek the engineer or the nearest building, chew through blocking buildings (walls are real blockers); buildings have HP (wall 200, turret 120, others 60) and are destroyed without refund. Biters show health bars; kills are counted.
- **Gun Turret (new building, select with U):** range 6.5 tiles, 12 damage per shot, consumes Ammo Magazines (buffer 5), 10 shots per magazine. Craft cost 8 iron plate + 4 iron gear.
- **Ammo Magazine (new item):** hand-craft for 2 iron plates, deliberately NOT research-gated (BeltAndSteam lesson); the assembler does not make it in this version (see TODO). Starting kit gains 1 turret + 2 magazines.
- **Engineer combat:** 100 HP, left-click shoots the nearest biter/nest within 7.5 tiles when nothing is selected (auto-loads magazines, 1 = 10 rounds); death respawns at the map centre with full HP.
- **Victory:** destroying all nests shows a victory message and the sandbox continues. Nests, biters, HP, rounds, and wave state are stored in saves; nests and biters appear on the minimap; the top bar shows HP / nests / wave.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: import clean, 300-frame run clean, feature harness 92/92 (68 prior + 24 new enemy checks), single-threaded Web export verified (GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false).

versions.title: Self-directed iteration run
versions.notes:
Self-directed iteration run, version 1 of the roadmap (per Josh's 2026-10-14 mandate) - coal finds a job, plus crafting depth:

- **Coal Generator (new building, select with G):** burns coal from its buffer - 1 coal = 10 s burn, contributes 25 generation while burning or while coal is buffered (first-guess balance). Craft cost 6 iron plate + 2 iron gear + 4 stone. Feedable by belt + inserter (accepts coal only, buffer 10); hover readout shows coal count and burn time; generator fuel state and the crafting queue are saved.
- **Timed hand-crafting queue (replaces instant crafting):** the C panel queues items (cost paid up front, max 10 queued), the front item crafts over time (2.0 s for buildings, 0.8 s for items - first-guess timings) and is delivered with a message; clicking a queued item cancels it with a full refund. An instant `craft_hand` helper remains only as an internal shortcut.
- **Hand mining:** hold left-click on a resource patch with nothing selected to mine by hand (0.7 s per item, mining progress percentage on the hover line).
- **TODO reconciled:** the v0.1.0 export-binaries P1 is Done - the zip-link watcher verified the binaries in git (commit 6577c4df).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: import clean, 300-frame run clean, feature harness 68/68 (see the export README), single-threaded Web export verified (GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false).

versions.title: Initial playable build
versions.notes:
Initial playable build - a new Factorio-like with 3D graphics on a 2D grid, built as a separate game next to BeltAndSteam (brighter, cleaner art, peaceful sandbox):

- 48x48 world, flat ground with a painted grid, deterministic resource patches (seed 12345): iron ore, copper ore, coal, stone.
- Engineer avatar (WASD), angled top-down perspective camera that follows the engineer, mouse-wheel zoom, R rotates the selected building.
- Mouse-ray grid cursor with a green/red placement ghost and a hover readout; left-click places, right-click hold (0.4 s) deconstructs with a full refund, X toggles demolish mode.
- Buildings (all 1x1): Miner, Conveyor Belt, Inserter, Furnace, Assembler, Chest, Lab, Solar Panel, Power Pole, Stone Wall - chunky BoxMesh visuals in distinct colours, with spinning parts on working machines and a visible item cube on belts.
- Items: iron ore, copper ore, coal, stone, iron plate, copper plate, iron gear, copper cable, red science.
- Simulation: belts hold 1 item and forward it when the next cell accepts; inserters swing items from the cell behind to the cell in front; miners output to their front cell or buffer; furnaces smelt ore to plate (powered, no fuel in v0.1.0); assemblers craft gears, cable, and red science.
- Solar power: panels generate 10, poles project coverage (radius 4), consumers draw Miner 5 / Furnace 5 / Assembler 8 / Inserter 1 / Lab 10, and satisfaction (generation / consumption, capped at 1) scales machine speed.
- Hand crafting (C) is instant with a cost check; research (T) has 3 techs fed by red science in labs - Logistics (belt/inserter speed x1.5), Efficiency (power use -30 percent), Advanced Automation (assembler speed x1.5). Completing all three shows a goal message; the sandbox continues.
- HUD: hotbar (1-0), inventory line, power and research readouts, version label, hover readout, message line, live minimap.
- Pause menu (Tab/Esc) with Help, the embedded Version Log, and named Save/Load; F5 quicksave / F9 quickload; saves are JSON at user://saves/.
- No enemies in v0.1.0 (see TODO.md P1).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: import clean, 300-frame run with no script errors, feature harness (see the export README for the final count), single-threaded Web export verified (GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false).

versions.title: Fair enemy hitbox fix
versions.notes:
Fair enemy hitbox fix, from Josh's playtest report ("enemies hit me before they should; I can't swing over them once they're below my crowd"):

- **Root cause in v0.1.0:** contact was a fixed rectangle — an enemy triggered when its center was still 60 px above the crowd and up to 78 px to either side (wider than a small crowd really is), and the test had no lower bound, so it kept triggering for as long as the enemy was on screen, including after it had scrolled below the crowd.
- **Circle contact, sized by the crowd:** contact now requires the enemy's center within `contact_distance` of the crowd's center — the enemy radius and the crowd's actual formation radius, both shrunk to 85% of the drawn size, with the crowd radius capped at 64 px. Small crowds are far harder to clip; hits always look like hits.
- **Passed enemies are harmless:** an enemy whose center scrolls past the crowd's line (`PLAYER_Y + 6`) without touching is marked passed, drawn faded, and can never damage the crowd — swinging over or across it afterwards is safe.
- Harness grew from 49 to 61 checks: crowd-radius and contact-distance values, a grazing enemy inside the old rectangle that must not hit, an enemy scrolled past in another column that must not hit when the crowd swings onto it, and a dead-center enemy that still costs its remaining HP.
- Validated: headless import clean, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness 61/61, single-threaded Web export verified (`GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false`).

versions.title: Initial playable build
versions.notes:
Initial playable build — a mobile-ad style endless crowd runner, phone-first:

- Portrait 540x960 (9:16) playfield, touch drag steering (mouse drag and A/D / arrow keys also work), large tap-to-start and run-again buttons, GL Compatibility renderer.
- Crowd auto-runs upward forever and auto-shoots upward; bullet damage scales with crowd size (1 + 1 per 8 members).
- Gate pairs: steer through one gate per row — `+5` / `+10` / `+15` / `+20`, `x2` / `x3`, negative gates `-3` / `-5` / `-10` / `-15`, and `/2`. The first gate pair is a gentle `+10` vs `+5`.
- Numbered enemies block the track; an enemy that reaches the crowd alive damages the crowd by its remaining HP and is destroyed. Dodging an enemy avoids the damage entirely.
- Boss enemy every 5th event; run speed (255 to 430 px/s) and enemy HP scale with distance.
- HUD with crowd count, distance, and kills; floating gate/collision feedback; game-over screen with run stats; best distance saved to `user://`.
- Validated: headless import clean, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness (see SPENDING.md / export README for the count), single-threaded Web export verified (`GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false`).

versions.title: Deploy screen
versions.notes:
- Deploy now opens a deploy screen first: who's going (and who comes along), what they'll carry, the zone (biome, danger, weather, contract, distress call, radio), its threats if you have a watchtower, and how fast infection will build for this survivor.
- The infection line counts their Resist skill, cures, vaccines, specialisation and a partner, and says how long on purple ground until Critical; a respirator is mentioned when you'll carry one.
- Go starts the run; Back to camp lets you change your mind.

versions.title: Conditions
versions.notes:
- Zones now have weather for the next run, rolled after every run (half the time there's none): rain, fog or a blackout. The world map shows it on the zone and says what it does.
- Rain: your footsteps make half the noise, but blooms spread the infected ground twice as far. Fog: you and the infected both see less far. Blackout: darker, you see less, and containers hold batteries.
- Every condition puts extra loot in three containers. A tip explains each the first time, and the HUD names the condition.

versions.title: Shriekers
versions.notes:
- New infected from the second ring of zones: the shrieker, tall, pale and frail. When it spots you it glows and rears back for a moment, then screams, and every infected within 18 m comes for you.
- Hit it while it rears (an arrow, a rock, a shove) to cut the scream off. It can scream again after 12 seconds.
- A tip explains it the first time one rears, and that first one takes twice as long to scream.

versions.title: New player model
versions.notes:
- Survivors are now proper figures instead of capsules: a head, a torso in their colour, legs that swing as they walk, arms (one holds the bow or pistol) and a backpack.
- Crouching leans the body forward; a respirator shows as a mask.
- Survivors you rescue, partners and settlers in safe zones use the same figure.
- Low graphics keeps the figures but skips the walk swing.

versions.title: Survivor roster
versions.notes:
- The camp's survivor list is now one short line each (colour, name, status, infection bar, level) in a column that only scrolls up and down.
- Click a line to see that survivor in full below the list, with all their actions (quarantine, treat, cure, bring along, skill points, specialising).
- Choose on a line (or Choose for this run in the details) picks who deploys; the line says Going.

versions.title: Save export and import
versions.notes:
- Export a save as text: Save slots > Export / import on the title screen, or Save: export / import at camp. It's copied to the clipboard too, so you can keep it safe or move it to another browser.
- Import pastes a save back into any slot. Replacing a slot that has a save asks you to press Import again first.
- Text that isn't a save (a run log, a cut-off paste) is refused with the reason; saves from older versions import and get the newer fields filled in.

**Limitations:** Export and import go through a text box and the clipboard; there's no file download yet.

versions.title: Save slots
versions.notes:
- Three save slots. The title screen has Save slots: each shows its runs, survivors, safe zones and when it was last saved, with Continue, New game and Delete (both ask first if they'd lose a save).
- New game starts in the first empty slot; Continue loads the slot you played last.
- Your existing save moves into slot 1 automatically, untouched.
- A small "Saved (slot N)" note shows at camp and on the run summary each time the game saves, so you know progress is kept in the browser.

versions.title: Run log
versions.notes:
- Run log at camp: every run you finish is kept (the last 30) with its route and what happened on it. Pick one to replay its route on the map.
- Delete runs you don't want, Export the log as text (also copied to the clipboard) and Import a log someone pasted, without doubling runs you already have.

versions.title: Route replay
versions.notes:
- The map on the run summary now replays your route: the line draws itself over a few seconds, and each moment (searched, kill, subdued, sedated, recruited, heart) pops up with its letter as the line reaches it.
- Click the map to skip to the end, or Replay route to watch it again.

versions.title: Web performance
versions.notes:
- Faster busy fights, especially in the browser: infected vision cones are worked out again only when an infected moves or turns (about 9 times less work a frame with a crowd).
- Infected ground, the fog of war and mushroom clumps redraw only what changed, and arrows and spit reuse their meshes instead of making new ones.

versions.title: Graphics setting
versions.notes:
- Settings has a Graphics option: Low (faster) turns off shadows, spore particles and the vision cones of infected more than 8 m away, for slower machines and browsers.
- An optional FPS counter (Settings) shows frames a second in the top right.

versions.title: Camp walkthrough
versions.notes: - The first time you come back to camp, a short walkthrough frames quarantine, the cure, the workbench and the world map one at a time, with a line on each. Next moves on; Skip ends it.

versions.title: Guided first run
versions.notes:
- A guided first run: a small training ground that walks you through moving, shooting the bow, searching a crate, crossing infected ground and extracting, one prompt at a time.
- New players get it from the title screen (Play) or can skip it; it's always there as Guided first run. Nothing from it goes into your save.
- The pause menu's list of controls sits on its own panel, and the controls line at the bottom of a run fits the screen.

versions.title: Key rebinding
versions.notes:
- Rebind every key in Settings > Controls: click an action, then press its new key (Esc cancels). Taking a key another action uses swaps the two; Reset to defaults puts them back.
- The pause menu lists your controls, and the hint line at the bottom of a run follows your bindings.

**Limitations:** Tips still name the default keys.

versions.title: Minimap
versions.notes:
- A minimap in the bottom right shows the part of the zone you've explored, turned to match the camera, with infected ground in purple.
- It marks the exit (green), containers you've seen (yellow, grey once searched), spore hearts you've seen (red), and you with the way you're aiming.

versions.title: The outbreak's story
versions.notes:
- Every zone hides one note in a container. Get it home and it goes in the journal at camp (Journal button), telling where the mushroom came from.
- With 6 notes the journal points to the source of the outbreak, deep in the hardest open zone (SOURCE on the world map): a giant red spore heart.
- Arrows and blades can't hurt the source; only fire on the ground at its roots (a torch or fire arrows) burns it out. A tip explains it when you get there.

versions.title: Distress calls
versions.notes:
- Distress calls: after a run, a survivor may call for help from one of the open zones. The world map marks it with ! and the runs left.
- Go there within 2 runs: the caller is always somewhere in the zone, and the HUD reminds you to find them. Bring them home and they join the camp with 2 medicine.
- Leave it too long and the call goes silent.

versions.title: Camp requests
versions.notes:
- Survivors at camp ask for things: 5 food, 3 medicine, a pistol, 15 arrows, 4 parts, 3 spore samples, or a rescue. Two requests are open at a time, in a new Requests section at camp.
- Give what they ask from the stash for a reward: XP or a skill point for the one who asked, or rare gear (broadhead arrows, a vaccine, filters or batteries).
- A rescue request is filled when a run brings a survivor home. A new request comes in after each run.

versions.title: Specialisations
versions.notes:
- At level 5 a survivor specialises: pick one of two upgrades to their perk on their card at camp.
- Scout: Ghost (sprinting is as quiet as walking) or Keen eyes (see 3 m farther). Brute: Bulwark (+25 health) or Thick skin (hits infect 30% less).
- Medic: Field medic (also heals recruits and party members near you) or Quick heal (heals sooner and twice as fast). Botanist: Spore ward (infected ground infects 25% slower) or Collector (three times the spore samples).
- Marksman: Deadeye (focused hits +100%) or Quickdraw (draws the bow 30% faster). Forager: Scavenger (searches 30% faster) or Packer (three times the sticks and food).

versions.title: Trust
versions.notes:
- Survivors build trust with each other: every run two of them finish together (leader and party member) adds one, and a survivor you rescue starts out trusting whoever brought them home.
- At 3 trust a party member is trusted: they move faster when you give orders, hand you 3 arrows when you run dry, and add only half the usual infection liability. A tip explains it the first time.
- Survivor cards at camp list who they trust.

versions.title: Party of two
versions.notes:
- Bring along a second ready survivor from camp (Bring along on their card): they come on the run as a party member who follows your orders and shoots with up to 10 arrows from the stash.
- They bring their skills: Health gives them more health, Aim makes their arrows hit harder, Resist slows their infection. Like any recruit, they make infection build faster for the party.
- Party members earn XP (half the run's), keep the infection they picked up, and bring their pack home if they're with you at the exit. If they fall they come home wounded; if they turn, they're gone.
- Survivors you rescue now earn XP on the run they join, so recruits level up like everyone else.

versions.title: Conveyor belts
versions.notes:
- Join two neighbouring safe zones with a conveyor belt (2 parts, 3 scrap), from the selected zone's supplies at camp.
- Every run a belt moves up to 2 supply from the better-stocked end to the other, and carries the far zone's goods to the zone nearer camp. Chain belts and a single supply line to a near zone keeps far zones stocked.
- Zones on a belt show = on the world map. A belt stops if either end falls.

versions.title: Reclaim moment
versions.notes: - When a run makes a zone safe, the camp's world map celebrates it: the zone's purple shrinks away and it glows green, with a rising sting.

versions.title: Reclaimed zones look reclaimed
versions.notes: - Going back into a safe zone now shows the progress: the ground has grown back green, fences stand round the start and the extraction, lamps light the way, and a few settlers stroll about.

versions.title: Camp buildings
versions.notes:
- Build up the camp with scavenged materials. Each building is bought once.
- Greenhouse (4 scrap, 2 parts, 2 food): grows 1 food every run.
- Lab (4 scrap, 2 parts, 3 chemicals): cures and research cost 1 spore sample less.
- Watchtower (6 scrap, 2 parts): the world map tells you which infected and hazards wait in a zone (and who turned there) before you deploy.
- Storeroom (5 scrap, 3 cloth): runs take half as much gear again: 30 arrows, 36 rounds, more filters, batteries, lanterns and special arrows.

versions.title: Quarantine ward
versions.notes:
- The quarantine ward has beds now: 2 to start with, so you can't quarantine everyone at once. Add more at camp (3 scrap, 1 part each, up to 6).
- Treatment: switch it on for a quarantined survivor and they recover twice as fast (24% a run instead of 12%), for 1 medicine a run while you have some.
- The camp shows how many beds are in use; survivor cards show who's being treated.

versions.title: Cure research
versions.notes:
- Research at camp, paid in spore samples, unlocks things for good.
- Refined cure (4 spore samples): cures cost 2 spore samples and 1 medicine instead of 3 and 2.
- Suppressant (3 spore samples): make suppressants (1 spore sample, 1 chemicals). Give one to a survivor at camp and their infection can't grow at all on their next run.
- Vaccine (6 spore samples, 1 medicine): make vaccines (2 spore samples, 1 medicine). A vaccinated survivor takes 40% less infection for 3 runs.
- Survivor cards show who's suppressed or vaccinated.

versions.title: The lost return
versions.notes:
- A survivor overrun by the infection now comes back in the zone where they turned: a named, tougher infected (150 health, harder claws) still carrying everything they had on them.
- The world map shows who turned in each zone, and the zone note lists what they carry, before you go back in. The first time you see one, a tip names them.
- Put them down (kill or subdue) and their gear drops where they fall. Extract afterwards and they're laid to rest; fail the run and they'll be back.

versions.title: Radio posts
versions.notes:
- Some zones have a radio post (R on the world map: Rail Yard, Orchard, Stadium, Greenhouses, The Bloom). It's a crate with a tall mast and a blinking red lamp, and a tip points it out early in the run.
- Press E at the radio to call in another ready survivor. Whoever is out there goes home with everything they carry and the sealed pouch (plus a little XP), keeping their infection; the new survivor takes over at the radio with their own loadout.
- One call a run. Use it to rotate out a survivor whose infection is climbing without losing the run.

versions.title: Puffball mines
versions.notes:
- Puffballs grow on infected ground in the harder zones (from Rail Yard on): fat pale caps that pulse and glow once you're within 4 m.
- Step on one (or right next to it) and it bursts into a spore cloud: a big jump in infection and freshly infected ground round it.
- Shoot one from a distance, or burn it, to clear it safely.
- The first zone you find them in shows a tip as soon as one glows, and keeps them out in the open, away from the mushroom clumps.

versions.title: Lurkers
