versions.notes:
- A new infected: lurkers hide inside mushroom clumps in the harder zones (one or more a run from Rail Yard on).
- They give themselves away: within 5 m their clump twitches and puffs spores, and the first time you see one a tip explains it.
- Get within 2 m after the twitching starts and the lurker lunges at you. Shooting the clump flushes it out first; noises don't move it.

versions.title: Light and the infected
versions.notes:
- Light now changes how some infected behave, and you find out by trying it (a tip explains each one the first time you see it happen).
- Runners can't stand the flashlight: one caught in the beam is blinded for 2 s and staggers on the spot (the same runner can't be dazzled again for a few seconds).
- Spitters are drawn to light: they drift toward lanterns, and toward you while your flashlight is on.
- Shamblers standing in lantern light calm down: they get suspicious much more slowly.

versions.title: Lanterns
versions.notes:
- Make lanterns at the workbench (2 scrap, 1 fuel). A run takes up to 3.
- B sets one down where you stand. It lights 5 m round it, and the zone keeps it for every later run (up to 8 a zone), even if this run goes wrong. Dark places get safer the more you light them.
- In the dark, lantern-lit ground shows from up to 13 m away, so you can see what's waiting in the light.
- The camp's world map counts the lanterns lit in each zone. The flashlight beam is brighter.

versions.title: Flashlight
versions.notes:
- Make a flashlight (2 parts, 1 scrap) and batteries (1 part makes 2) at the workbench. A run takes the flashlight and up to 3 batteries.
- L switches it on: a 70 degree cone of light where you aim lets you see out to 13 m, even in the dark subways where you'd otherwise see 7 m.
- The catch: infected see the beam. Any infected it shines on notices you whichever way it faces, and the rest spot you from half again as far while it's on.
- A battery lasts 90 s switched on; a spare is fitted when one runs flat, and the light goes out when they're all spent. The HUD shows what's left.

versions.title: Biomes
versions.notes:
- Every zone now has a biome with its own ground, walls, light and loot: ruins (as before), fungal forest (dense mushroom clumps, more sticks and food), flooded subway (dark: you only see 7 m; chemicals and parts), hospital (tight rooms; medicine and cloth) and greenhouse farm (food and spore samples).
- The camp's world map tells you a zone's biome before you deploy, and warns when you'll see less there. The dark subways are only in the harder zones (Water Works, Mill District).
- The HUD shows the biome next to the zone name.

versions.title: Machete
versions.notes:
- Make a machete at the workbench (3 scrap, 2 parts). A run takes it along.
- With the machete out, F is a quiet slash: infected that haven't noticed you die on the spot, aware ones take a 30 damage cut (brutes only ever take the cut).
- Slashing cuts down the mushroom clumps in front of you, clearing their spores, and sometimes gathers a spore sample.
- M puts the machete away so F shoves again (for subduing instead of killing).

versions.title: Burn it back
versions.notes:
- Fire: fire arrows and the new torch (T, 1 fuel: sets the ground 2.6 m in front of you alight) burn infected ground clean for the rest of the run, leaving it scorched.
- Fire is loud and creeps into neighbouring mushroom ground. Small yellow flames show where it will catch 1.5 s before it does; clean ground doesn't burn.
- Standing in fire hurts you, your recruits and infected alike. A tip explains fire the first time you start one.
- The tip line moved right so it no longer covers the health bars.

versions.title: Arrow types
versions.notes:
- Three new arrows from the workbench: broadheads (2 scrap, 1 stick for 3) hit 60% harder but always break; noise arrows (1 parts, 1 stick for 3) do no damage and make a racket where they land, pulling infected away from you; fire arrows (1 cloth, 1 fuel, 1 stick for 3) burn the infected ground clean where they land.
- R now cycles sharp, blunt and any special arrows you carry. When the last special arrow is gone, the bow goes back to sharp.
- A run takes up to 6 of each special arrow. Special arrows can't be picked up again.

versions.title: Flare extraction
versions.notes:
- A second way out: with fuel in your pack, press X to fire a flare right where you stand (1 fuel, once a run).
- The flare is loud: every 4 s it calls every infected within 20 m. Hold inside its red ring for 20 s in all (time outside doesn't count) and you're picked up there.
- Recruits near the flare come home with you. The first time you carry fuel, a tip explains the flare.

versions.title: Spore bloom
versions.notes:
- Runs now have a clock: 3 minutes in, the zone blooms, and again every 90 s after. Each bloom spreads infected ground outward and wakes more infected near the spore hearts, out of your sight.
- The HUD counts down to the next bloom, and the screen warns you 30 s before each one (the first time with a tip).
- The three containers farthest from the extraction are deep: they hold more loot. Staying for them is the gamble.
- Safe zones don't bloom.

versions.title: Respirators and filters
versions.notes:
- Craft a respirator (2 cloth, 2 parts) and filters (1 cloth, 1 chemicals) at the workbench.
- A run takes your respirator and up to 3 filters. While a filter lasts (60 s of breathing on infected ground each), infection from the ground is halved; a spare is fitted when one runs out.
- The HUD shows how much filter is left. Like other gear, the respirator is lost if the run is (seal it in the pouch to be safe).

versions.title: Symptoms
versions.notes:
- From Exposed on, survivors cough now and then (more often as the infection grows). A cough is a noise enemies hear from 6 m.
- The screen warns you a second before each cough: crouch (C) to cover your mouth and muffle it to 2 m. Muffled, not silent, so Exposed survivors still carry a risk.
- Critical survivors see phantom shamblers at the edge of their sight: faint, flickering, harmless, and they fade if you look straight at them.
- New one-time tips at the top of the screen explain each symptom before it matters (the first cough comes 8 s after its tip). Tips show once per save.

versions.title: Infection on screen
versions.notes:
- A purple vignette closes in from the screen edges as your infection grows, and spores drift across the screen from Exposed on.
- At Critical you hear your heartbeat and the vignette throbs with it.
- Infected pop in a puff of spores when they die (a smaller puff when subdued).

versions.title: Sounds
versions.notes:
- New sounds for recruiting and healing survivors, searching (a rustle while you search, a clunk when it opens), spitters spitting and their globs splatting, bloated bursting, sealing the pouch, and meeting a contract.
- Sounds far from you are quieter, and ones more than 28 m away aren't heard at all.

versions.title: Zone contracts
versions.notes:
- Open zones offer a contract for their next run ($ on the world map): bring back 3 spore samples, search 5 containers, bring a survivor home, destroy a spore heart, or extract without killing anyone.
- Meet it and extract to get paid: materials and XP. A new contract appears there afterwards.
- The HUD shows the contract's progress on the run, and the run summary says whether it paid out. Sealed spore samples count.
- A rescue contract always has someone to rescue.

versions.title: Run summary
versions.notes:
- After every run a summary screen before camp: how it ended, what you brought home (items new to the stash marked NEW), infection gained, XP and any level up, kills, subdues, containers searched and spore hearts destroyed.
- A map of the zone shows the route you took, with where you searched, killed, subdued, recruited, lost a survivor or destroyed a heart.

versions.title: Sealed pouch
versions.notes:
- A sealed pouch with 2 slots: press P on a run to seal the item you found last (up to 5 of one item a slot). What's sealed comes home even if you die, are overrun or pull out.
- Sealed items can't be used on the run (seal arrows and you can't shoot them).
- Upgrade the pouch at the workbench to 3 and then 4 slots (3 cloth, 2 parts each).

versions.title: Hit feedback
versions.notes:
- Arrows and bullets knock enemies back a little (brutes barely budge), and every hit flashes white.
- You flash when hurt, the screen edges flash red, and claws, pistol shots, bursts and dying hearts shake the camera.
- Spore hearts flash when hit.

versions.title: Noise meter
versions.notes:
- A ring on the ground around you shows how far your last noise carried: any enemy inside it comes to look. It turns from white to red as you get louder and fades when you're quiet.
- A Noise bar under Infection shows the same in metres (silent, walking 3 m, sprinting 7 m, a pistol shot 16 m).

versions.title: Logistics lines
versions.notes:
- Safe zones now need supplies to stay safe: each uses 1 a run (it starts with 6, up to 10). The world map shows every safe zone's supply.
- Out of supply, a zone stops pushing the infection back, and after 3 unsupplied runs it falls: one spore heart regrows. The camp warns you each run before that happens.
- Supply a zone by hand from camp (1 fuel and 1 food for +3), or put a survivor on a supply line: each run they bring the zone's goods home and carry +1 supply in, or +3 if there's fuel for the truck. Runners can't deploy; Recall brings them back.
- Every supplied safe zone makes something each run (food, parts, scrap, fuel, medicine...), waiting there until a supply line collects it.

**Limitations:** Supply lines run between camp and one safe zone; there are no conveyor belts or zone-to-zone lines yet.

versions.title: More enemy types
versions.notes:
- Runners (orange caps): fragile but faster than you walk.
- Bloated (swollen, yellow): slow, and they burst into a spore cloud when they die or reach you, soaking the ground and anyone close in infection. Shoot them from a distance.
- Spitters (green, from the second ring of zones): keep their distance, back off if you close in, and spit spores from up to 7.5 m.
- Mycelium brutes (big and dark, from harder zones): 220 health, hit hard, and can't be shoved or taken down.
- Harder zones mix in more kinds; the Outskirts only has shamblers, runners and bloated.

versions.title: Scavenging
versions.notes:
- Zones hold crates, cabinets, wrecked cars and bodies to search. Press E to start searching; stay close and don't get hurt until it's done.
- Each kind has its own loot: cabinets hold medicine, cloth and chemicals; cars hold parts, fuel and scrap; bodies hold food, cloth, ammo and spores.
- Searching takes time: 1 s for a crate up to 3 s for a car. Cars are noisy to search, and bodies breathe spores at you.
- The camp workbench makes medicine (cloth, chemicals), pistol ammo (parts, chemicals) and a pistol (parts, scrap), as well as arrows.

versions.title: Rescue survivors
versions.notes:
- Most runs in an unsafe zone have a survivor waiting somewhere for help. Press E by them to recruit them.
- Recruits follow you; G tells them all to hold where they stand or follow again.
- By a recruit: E takes what they carry like a chest, V gives them 5 arrows (they shoot infected within 8 m), H heals them with 1 medicine.
- The catch: every recruit makes infection build 25% faster for the whole party. Recruits pick up infection too; at 100% they turn into one of the infected.
- Extract with recruits close by and they join the camp with their own perk; anyone left far from the extraction stays behind.
- E, V, H and G now act once per key press.

versions.title: Limited vision
versions.notes:
- Your own vision needs line of sight: you see 13 m all round, but not through walls.
- What you cannot see is dark; ground you have seen this run stays dimly lit. Infected, their vision cones and dropped items only show while you can see them.
- You can only focus (cursor bonus) on infected you can see.

versions.title: Docile infected
versions.notes:
- Stand by a subdued infected and press E to sedate it (1 medicine). It turns docile and follows you.
- Extract with it and it joins the camp. Docile infected train for 3 runs (1 food each a run).
- Trained ones can come on your next run as a companion (choose on the camp screen): it follows you and claws infected within 5 m. Infected fight back; a companion that falls is gone.
- Subdued and dazed infected no longer show vision cones.

versions.title: Lethal and non-lethal
versions.notes:
- F shoves: an enemy that has not spotted you is knocked out on the spot (a takedown); one that is chasing you is knocked back and dazed. Costs stamina.
- R swaps the bow between sharp and blunt arrows. Blunt arrows subdue instead of killing, and never break.
- Subdued infected lie on the ground, harmless, for 30 seconds before they get up. You can still kill them.
- Camp counts infected killed and subdued; subdues earn the same XP as kills.

**Limitations:** Subdued infected only get back up for now; sedating and training them comes next.

versions.title: Perks
versions.notes:
- Every survivor has a perk that changes how they play, shown on their camp card.
- Mara, Scout: walks silently and crouches faster. Okafor, Brute: +30 health, 40% less claw damage. Lin, Medic: heals after 4 seconds unhurt. Dace, Botanist: double spore samples.
- Newcomers can also be a Marksman (+50% focused damage) or Forager (double sticks and food).
- Pushed-back zones now lose infection more evenly.

versions.title: Safe zones expand
versions.notes:
- Safe zones push the infection back: every run, each open zone next to a safe zone loses 6% of its infection (shown as -% on the world map), up to 70%. Pushed-back zones also have fewer infected.
- Build an outpost in a safe zone (6 scrap, 2 food) to double its push.
- The camp shows how much of the world is reclaimed.

versions.title: Safe zones and the world map
versions.notes:
- A world map of 12 zones at camp. Pick where the next run goes; each zone keeps its layout between runs.
- Spore hearts: pulsing growths at the heart of each zone infection. Shoot one to destroy it and the ground around it is cleansed (it also wakes nearby enemies).
- Destroy every heart in a zone and extract: it becomes a permanent safe zone, with clean ground and no infected, and the zones next to it open.
- Hearts destroyed on a run you extract from stay destroyed; die and they grow back. Further zones have more hearts and more enemies.

versions.title: Skills and levels
versions.notes:
- Survivors earn XP on runs: 10 per kill, 5 per crate, 25 for extracting (failed runs give half).
- Each level gives a skill point to spend at camp on the survivor card: Health (+15 max health), Resist (12% slower infection) or Aim (steadier aim, +15% focus damage). Up to 5 in each.
- Camp cards show level, XP and skills.

versions.title: Stealth
versions.notes:
- Enemies see in a cone (drawn on the ground) that walls block. The cone turns from yellow to red as they notice you; they only attack once it fills.
- Anything within 1.5 m is noticed whatever way they face.
- C toggles crouch: half speed, silent, and enemies see you from only 60% as far. Sprinting stands you up.
- Noise draws enemies to look: walking (2.5 m), sprinting (7 m), the pistol (16 m), the bow (2.5 m), arrows hitting walls.
- Q throws a rock at the cursor (up to 10 m). Enemies near where it lands go to look.

versions.title: Bow and arrows
versions.notes:
- The starter weapon is a bow: hold left click to draw, release to shoot. A full draw hits about three times harder and flies faster.
- Arrows land where they stop and can be picked up again (some break in bodies).
- Sticks lie around every zone, every run. At camp, craft 4 arrows from 2 sticks and 1 scrap. Deploying with no arrows gives you 5 makeshift ones.
- Pistols are rare crate finds: 2 to switch to it, 1 back to the bow. It fires while held and needs ammo.
- Each run takes up to 20 arrows, and the pistol with up to 24 rounds. Gear is lost if the run is.

versions.title: Cursor focus damage
versions.notes:
- Put the cursor right on an enemy to focus it: a red ring marks it, and shots fired while focused deal 75% more damage when they hit it (like Escape from Duckov).
- Damage numbers float up from hits; focused hits show in gold.

versions.title: Mushroom infected enemies
versions.notes:
- Shamblers: people overgrown by the mushroom infection. They wander infected ground, chase you when they see you, and route around walls.
- Their claws hurt and add infection. Health at zero means you are killed and the loot is lost.
- Shots kill them (3 hits). Some drop spore samples; walk over drops to pick them up.
- Shot enemies come looking for you; enemies that lose sight keep tracking you for a few seconds.

**Limitations:** One enemy type so far. They see all around them; vision cones and stealth come later.

versions.title: Quarantine and the cure
versions.notes:
- Quarantine a survivor at camp: they cannot deploy, eat 1 food a run and lose 12% infection a run (only 5% if there is no food).
- Critical survivors (75%+) left outside quarantine get worse every run and turn at 100%.
- Brew a cure from 3 spore samples and 2 medicine. Only a cure clears infection for good, and the survivor gains infection at half rate for their next 3 runs.

**Limitations:** Still no enemies; they arrive next.

versions.title: Extraction and the camp
versions.notes:
- A camp between runs: four survivors, each with their own infection. Choose who deploys.
- Crates in the zone (E to open). Crates on infected ground hold more, including spore samples.
- Stand in the green extraction ring for 3 seconds to extract and keep your loot. Dying or being overrun loses it.
- Survivors who sit out a run recover 5% infection, so rotate them. Killed survivors are wounded for two runs; overrun survivors turn and are gone.
- The camp is saved. Title screen: Continue or New game. Pause menu: Abandon run.
- Walls are lower so they no longer hide you.

**Limitations:** No enemies yet. Infection only comes down slowly by resting; quarantine and the cure are next.

versions.title: Infection on the body
versions.notes:
- Walking on infected ground builds infection on your character (0-100%), faster on worse ground. It does not go down in the field.
- Stages: Clean, Exposed, Infected, Critical. From Infected your aim wobbles; infection also slows stamina regen. The screen tints as it grows.
- At 100% the character is overrun and the run ends.
- Shift to sprint (uses stamina). Health, stamina and infection bars.

**Limitations:** Nothing heals infection yet; quarantine and the cure come in later versions.

versions.title: Isometric core
versions.notes:
- An isometric camera follows you through a generated zone of ruins, rubble and infected ground.
- WASD moves relative to the screen, the mouse aims, left click shoots. Shots stop at walls.
- Mushroom clumps grow on badly infected ground; the ground turns purple where the infection is.

**Limitations:** No enemies or goals yet: this is the movement and shooting core.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.
